statement: Finite coefficient data may be tensored with a finite category: Let $K$ be a finite connected polyhedron. The diagram obtained by tensoring these retractive spaces with $A$, and then applying finitely many products and finite homotopy colimits, has a model built from finite categories and functors. statement: The coefficient matrices and their controlled homotopies: Let $K$ be a finite connected CW complex of dimension $k$, with fundamental group $\pi$, and take $m>k+1$, $m\geq3$. statement: A3.5: Sch\"utzenberger induction and apex filtration: Let $M$ be a finite monoid, $k$ a field, and $e\in M$ idempotent. Consequently \[ \operatorname{Ind}_e W=kL_e\otimes_{kG_e}W \] is an exact functor from finite-dimensional $kG_e$-modules to finite-dimensional $kM$-modules. Every simple $kM$-module $S$ has an idempotent $e$, called an apex, for which $eS$ is a simple $kG_e$-module and there is an exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow\operatorname{Ind}_e(eS) \longrightarrow S\longrightarrow0. \tag{A.1} \] Every composition factor of $K$ has apex in a strictly larger regular $\mathcal J$-class, where $e\leq_{\mathcal J}f$ means $e\in MfM$.

statement: A3.7: local-group nilpotence detection: Let $C$ be a finite category and $k$ any field. For every idempotent $e\in\operatorname{End}_C(c)$, let $G_e$ be the group of units of $e\operatorname{End}_C(c)e$. The kernel of the graded ring homomorphism \[ H^*(BC;k)\longrightarrow\prod_{(c,e)}H^*(BG_e;k) \tag{A.3} \] is a nilpotent ideal. In particular a positive-degree homogeneous class is nilpotent if and only if its restriction to every $G_e$ is nilpotent. Equivalently one may test every subgroup of every local group. This proves the detection assertion of A3(i) for finite monoids as well.

statement: An explicit uniform exponent: The proof bounds the power of the entire kernel, not only a power of one class. For each simple module $S$ choose (A.1), and define recursively \[ a(S)=1+\sum_T[K:T]a(T). \] The sum runs over the simple composition factors of $K$, with multiplicity; the strictly larger apices make this a finite recursion. Then $J^{a(S)}$ annihilates $S$, and $N=\sum_S[\Delta k:S]a(S)$ is a valid nilpotence exponent in (A.3). There is also a rough bound depending only on the category. Put $q=|\operatorname{Ob}C|$, $t=|\operatorname{Mor}C|$, and let $r$ be the number of regular $\mathcal J$-classes of the consolidation monoid represented by actual arrows. For a nonempty category one may take \[ N\leq q\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}t^j. \] To check this, a simple $kG_e$-module is a quotient of its regular module, so has dimension at most $|G_e|$. Freeness of $L_e$ then gives $\dim\operatorname{Ind}_e(eS)\leq |L_e|\leq t$; hence each kernel has composition length at most $t$. Induction over at most $r$ successive apex levels gives the displayed geometric sum. Finally the total vector space dimension of $\Delta k$ is $q$, so its composition length is at most $q$. The empty category is vacuous.

If $e,f$ are idempotents satisfying $ef=fe=f$, then $P(e,f)=R(e-f)$ is projective, has basis \[ \{v-vf:v\in Me\setminus Mf\}, \] and left multiplication by $a$ sends this basis vector to $av-(av)f$ if $av\notin Mf$, and to zero otherwise. Tensoring with the trivial right module sends $P(e)$ to $\mathbb Z$ and $P(e,f)$ to zero.

statement: The integral projective certificates give the following resolutions and homology groups. The tuple in the third column records the underlying abelian ranks of $P_0,P_1,\ldots$; a repeated tail is marked explicitly. \[ \begin{array}{c|r|l|l} M&|M|&\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}P_*&\widetilde H_*(BM;\mathbb Z)\\ \hline A_2&7&(2,4,3)&\mathbb Z\text{ in degree }2\\ A_3&16&(2,8,10,3)&\mathbb Z\text{ in degree }3\\ M(\operatorname{sk}_2NC_2,*)&22&(4,10,12,5)&\mathbb Z/2\text{ in degree }2\\ M(Y_z,f_z)&175&(22,244,290,67)&0\\ M(Y_z,*)&175&(22,277,312,56)&\mathbb Z\text{ in degrees }2,3\\ M(S^1_\Delta,f_1)&11&(4,10,9,4,4,\ldots)&\text{as in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-finite-resolution-obstruction}}\\ M(S^1_\Delta,f_g)&11&(4,6,5,4,4,\ldots)&\text{as in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-finite-resolution-obstruction}}\\ M(\operatorname{sk}_2NC_2,\iota)&34&(8,14,12,9,8,8,\ldots)&\mathbb Z/2\text{ in odd degrees }\ge3 . \end{array} \] Every group not specified in the last column is zero. In each infinite resolution the tail is two-periodic as a complex of projective $\mathbb ZM$-modules.

statement: The twelve tetrahedra from the public supplement \cite{BenBassatSupplementB}, specified below, define a finite reduced simplicial set $Y\simeq S^3$ and a map $Y\to N(L_0)$ of Hopf invariant $1$. Consequently Definition~3.3 gives an associative $1795$-element monoid whose classifying space is $\mathbb{CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $K$ be a finite category, let $P:K\to\mathbf{Set}$ be a finite covariant functor, and suppose $P(d_0)$ is a singleton and every object of $K$ is a retract of $c_0$. Then there is a finite monoid \[ \operatorname{End}_K(c_0)\ \amalg\ \big(P(c_0)\times K(c_0,d_0)\big) \] whose classifying space is the homotopy cofiber of $B\operatorname{El}(P)\to BK$. The product of two elements in the second summand is $(p,\alpha)(p',\alpha')=(p,\alpha')$; the old monoid acts on the left through $P$ and on the right by precomposition on $\alpha$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The annulus construction of \cite{BenBassatSupplementB} gives an associative monoid of order $122$ with classifying space $\mathbb{CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Suppose the minimal ideal of $M$ is a rectangular band $K=I\times J$. Put $R=\mathbb ZM$, $A=R/\mathbb ZK$, $V=\ker(\mathbb ZI\to\mathbb Z)$ as a left module, and $W=\ker(\mathbb ZJ\to\mathbb Z)$ as a right module. Then \[ H_n(BM;\mathbb Z)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^{A}_{n-2}(W,V) \qquad(n\ge2). \] The same assertion holds after replacing $\mathbb Z$ by any field. In particular $H_2$ is the quotient of $W\otimes_{\mathbb Z}V$ by $wm\otimes v-w\otimes mv$ for $m\in M$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: If the minimal ideal of $M$ is a $2\times2$ rectangular band and $H_2(BM;\mathbb Z)$ has nonzero torsion, then $H_2(BM;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z/2$ and $H_n(BM;\mathbb F_2)\ne0$ for arbitrarily large $n$. Thus no such monoid is a finite-homotopy-type model of either torsion Moore space in Part~B4.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Suppose the minimal ideal of a finite monoid $M$ is a rectangular band with two rows or with two columns. If $BM$ has finite homotopy type, then every product of two integral degree-two cohomology classes is zero. In particular such a monoid cannot have classifying space $\CP^2$ or $S^2\times S^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let the minimal ideal of a finite monoid $M$ be the Rees matrix semigroup $K=I\times H\times J$. Collapse each of its $H$-classes to one element, leaving $M\setminus K$ unchanged, and call the resulting monoid $N$. The quotient homomorphism $q:M\to N$ induces a rational homology equivalence, hence an isomorphism of rational cohomology rings. The minimal ideal of $N$ is the rectangular band $I\times J$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: If the minimal ideal of a finite monoid has two rows or two columns, every product $H^2(BM;\mathbb Q)\otimes H^2(BM;\mathbb Q)\to H^4(BM;\mathbb Q)$ is zero. Neither finite homotopy type nor a trivial minimal maximal group is required.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $R_{r,s}^1$ be the monoid obtained by adjoining an identity to the $r$ by $s$ rectangular band. Then \[ BR_{r,s}^1\simeq\bigvee^{(r-1)(s-1)}S^2. \] Consequently the minimum order for $S^2\vee S^2$ is $7$, using the exhaustive lower-order census in Section~\ref{sec:C}.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The following nine-element monoid has classifying space $S^4$: \[ \begin{array}{c|ccccccccc} \cdot&1&a&b&c&d&u&v&w&t\\\hline 1&1&a&b&c&d&u&v&w&t\\ a&a&a&b&a&b&a&a&a&a\\ b&b&a&b&a&b&a&a&a&a\\ c&c&c&d&c&d&c&c&c&c\\ d&d&c&d&c&d&c&c&c&c\\ u&u&a&b&a&b&a&a&a&u\\ v&v&a&b&a&b&a&a&v&a\\ w&w&a&b&a&b&u&a&w&a\\ t&t&a&b&c&d&a&a&a&t \end{array} \] Together with the order-eight exclusion in the census, this proves that the minimum order for $S^4$ is $9$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: For each $n\ge2$ there is an explicit monoid $M_n$ of order $n^2+4n+1$ with $BM_n\simeq M(\mathbb Z/n,2)$ and a projective resolution of the trivial integral module of length three. In particular the orders $13$ and $22$ are certified upper bounds for the two torsion Moore spaces in Part~B4.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Computer-assisted Moore-space lower bound: Using the complete multiplication-table census in \cite{SweeneyEnumeration2026B}, no monoid of order at most twelve has classifying space $M(\mathbb Z/2,2)$ or $M(\mathbb Z/3,2)$. Consequently the minimum order for $M(\mathbb Z/2,2)$ is $13$, and the minimum for $M(\mathbb Z/3,2)$ is at least $13$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Complete source census with independently checked obstructions: Using the complete corner-irreducible table census of \cite{SweeneyEnumeration2026B}, no finite monoid of order at most twelve has classifying space $\CP^2$ or $S^2\times S^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Further complete restricted enumeration: No finite monoid of order at most fourteen has classifying space $\CP^2$ or $S^2\times S^2$. The enumeration-completeness dependency is the bounded-quotient source dataset of \cite{SweeneyEnumeration2026B}.

statement: A stronger lower bound for the odd Moore space: No finite monoid of order at most fourteen has classifying space $M(\mathbb Z/3,2)$. Thus its minimum order belongs to $[15,22]$. The source-census dependency is the same bounded-quotient dataset as in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-fourdim-lower14}.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A smaller explicit quotient: There is a $110$-element finite aperiodic monoid whose classifying space is $\CP^2$, with a complete integral projective resolution of length four.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A hundred-element model: There is a $100$-element finite aperiodic monoid of type $\CP^2$, with a complete projective resolution and an explicitly verified homology-equivalence inclusion into the preceding $110$-element model.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: An eighty-nine-element model: There is an $89$-element finite aperiodic monoid with classifying space $\CP^2$. Its complete projective resolution has length four, and its inclusion into the $110$-element model is an explicitly verified integral homology equivalence.

statement: A seventy-seven-element model: There is a $77$-element finite aperiodic monoid of type $\CP^2$, with a complete integral projective resolution of length four.

statement: All six minimum-order questions in Part~B4 are settled. Their exact values are $7$ for $S^2\vee S^2$, $9$ for $S^4$, $13$ for $M(\mathbb Z/2,2)$, $17$ for $M(\mathbb Z/3,2)$, $23$ for $\CP^2$, and $25$ for $S^2\times S^2$. Each upper bound has an explicit monoid and a complete homotopy identification; each matching lower bound records its structural and exhaustive finite-calculation dependencies above.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: If discrete monoids $M,N$ have homotopy-equivalent classifying spaces, there is a finite zigzag of unital monoid homomorphisms from $M$ to $N$, every arrow of which induces a homotopy equivalence of classifying spaces. The intermediate discrete monoids need not be finite. In particular, a finite monoid whose classifying space has finite homotopy type admits such a zigzag to a finite aperiodic monoid.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The literal endpoint requirement in Part~B5 is met by this proposition. Requiring every intermediate monoid to be finite is a stronger assertion, and the free resolution, group completion and discretization construction above does not prove it. It must not be inferred by replacing the words ``classifying spaces are equivalent'' with ``finite monoids are connected by equivalences''.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: There is a finite aperiodic monoid of order twenty-three whose classifying space is $\CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The exact minimum for the odd Moore space: The least order of a finite monoid whose classifying space is $M(\Z/3,2)$ is \textbf{17}. The upper-bound monoid is aperiodic. The lower bound uses the complete bounded-quotient source census specified in Proposition~\ref{prop:B-fourdim-lower14}, together with independent exact calculations and the structural exclusions proved here.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Third homology under a band-preserving quotient: Let $q:M\twoheadrightarrow N$ be a surjective homomorphism of finite monoids which restricts to a bijection between their rectangular-band minimal ideals. After identifying those ideals by $q$, the induced maps satisfy \[ H_2(BM;k)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }H_2(BN;k),\qquad H_3(BM;k)\twoheadrightarrow H_3(BN;k) \] for every commutative coefficient ring $k$, including $\mathbb Z$. In particular an actor image with nonzero third homology over a field cannot be the image of a projective-plane monoid of this kind, even when the action map is not faithful.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The invertible binary pencil case: Let $k$ be either $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $A_B$ be the four-dimensional $k$-algebra with basis $1,x,y,c$ and multiplication \[ x_i x_j=b_{ij}c,\qquad (x_1,x_2)=(x,y),\qquad c^2=cx=xc=cy=yc=0, \] where $B=(b_{ij})\in\operatorname{Mat}_2(\{0,1\})$ is invertible. For finite-dimensional right and left $A_B$-modules $W,V$, respectively, if $\operatorname{Tor}_2^{A_B}(W,V)\ne0$, then $\operatorname{Tor}_n^{A_B}(W,V)\ne0$ in arbitrarily high degrees.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $A$ be one of the two exceptional algebras in Proposition~\ref{B:five-nonlocal-exceptions}. Suppose that a right module $W$ and a left module $V$ satisfy \[ \dim V=2,\quad \dim W=4,\quad \dim\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(W,V)=0,\quad \dim\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)=1. \] For the zero-composite line algebra, the additional condition $\dim(W\otimes_A V)\leq2$ forces \[ V=S_1\oplus S_3,\qquad W=T_1\oplus T_3\oplus e_2A, \qquad \dim(W\otimes_A V)=2. \] Here $S_i$ and $T_i$ denote the left and right simple modules at vertex $i$. In particular this algebra cannot give the additive homology of $\CP^2$ through the band--Tor formula. For the Nakayama algebra, the conditions force \[ V=Ae_1/\Q c,\qquad W=T_2\oplus e_1A, \qquad \dim(W\otimes_A V)=1. \] The unique, up to scalar, balanced form $W\times V\to\Q$ has matrix rank one. Thus this algebra cannot give the additive homology of $S^2\times S^2$, and its degree-two square vanishes in every rectangular band realization by Lemma~\ref{B:rank-one-square}.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement:
An independent lower bound of twenty-one for
the projective plane: Every finite monoid whose classifying space is $\CP^2$ has at least twenty-one elements.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The multiplicative bases of the remaining line algebra: Suppose that a finite monoid $M$ has a $3\times5$ rectangular minimal band $K$, exactly five elements outside $K$, and $\Q M/\Q K$ is the zero-composite line algebra. If its band--Tor modules have the product pair in Lemma~\ref{B:five-exceptional-targets}, all rational products of degree-two classes on $BM$ vanish.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Every finite monoid whose classifying space is $S^2\times S^2$ has at least twenty-one elements.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The local five-dimensional target obstruction: Let $A$ be a local algebra over a field $k$, with $\dim_k A=5$ and $A/\operatorname{rad}(A)\cong k$. Let $W$ be a right $A$-module of dimension four and $V$ a left $A$-module of dimension two. The conditions \[ \dim_k(W\otimes_A V)\in\{1,2\},\qquad \operatorname{Tor}_1^A(W,V)=0,\qquad \dim_k\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)=1,\qquad \operatorname{Tor}_3^A(W,V)=0 \] cannot hold simultaneously.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The two nonlocal five-dimensional exceptions: Let $N$ be a finite monoid with zero, and let $A=\mathbb QN/\mathbb Q0$ have dimension five and be nonlocal. Then one of the following holds: \begin{enumerate} \item For all finite-dimensional right and left modules $W,V$, nonzero $\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)$ implies nonzero Tor in arbitrarily high degrees. \item $A$ is the radical-square-zero algebra of the line quiver $1\longrightarrow2\longrightarrow3$. \item $A$ is the two-vertex algebra with $a\in e_1Ae_2$, $b\in e_2Ae_1$, $ba=0$, and $ab=c\ne0$, where all products of $c$ with the radical are zero. \end{enumerate} In the second case the composite of the two arrows is zero. In the third case the projective lengths are three and two. The alternatives are statements about rational algebras; they do not prescribe a particular multiplicative monoid basis.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: No finite monoid of order at most twenty-two, with a $4\times4$ rectangular-band minimal ideal, has classifying space homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb{CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Four-by-four images under finite-target hypotheses: Let $M$ be a finite monoid with a $4\times4$ rectangular-band minimal ideal. Suppose \[ \dim_{\mathbb Q}H^2(BM;\mathbb Q)=1, \qquad H_3(BM;\mathbb Q)=0. \] Assume $H^2(BM;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Zv$, that the image of $v^2$ in $H^4(BM;\mathbb Z)$ modulo torsion is nonzero and primitive, and that every integral degree-two class restricts to zero on every local finite subgroup of $M$. Then the faithful row-and-column action image of $M$ has at least twenty-four elements. In particular, $|M|\leq23$ is impossible. No finite-CW hypothesis on $BM$ or on its action image is required, and $H_2(BM;\mathbb Z)$ may have torsion.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A finite monoid with a $4\times4$ minimal band and exactly five outside elements cannot have type $\CP^2$ or $S^2\times S^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Every finite monoid of type $\CP^2$ or $S^2\times S^2$ has at least twenty-two elements.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A lower bound on the faithful action image: If a finite monoid has a $4\times4$ rectangular-band minimal ideal and classifying space homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb CP^2$, its image in the monoid of row and column transformation pairs has at least twenty-four elements. This concerns the cardinality of the image, with no upper bound on the source monoid.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Minimal resolutions over a local algebra: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional local algebra over a field, and put $D=A/\operatorname{rad}(A)$. If a finite-dimensional right $A$-module $W$ is nonprojective, then \[ \operatorname{Tor}_n^A(W,D)\ne0\qquad(n\geq1). \] The analogous assertion holds for left modules.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The nonlocal four-dimensional case: Let $A$ be a nonlocal finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-algebra of dimension at most four. For finite-dimensional right and left modules $W,V$, respectively, nonzero $\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)$ implies nonzero $\operatorname{Tor}_n^A(W,V)$ in arbitrarily high degrees.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A one-dimensional simple target: Let $A$ be any finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-algebra with $\dim A\leq4$, let $W$ be a finite-dimensional right module, and let $V$ be a one-dimensional simple left module. If $\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)\ne0$, then $\operatorname{Tor}_n^A(W,V)\ne0$ for arbitrarily large $n$. The same conclusion holds with the sides interchanged.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Contracted algebras of dimension four: Let $N$ be a finite monoid with a zero element, and let $A=\mathbb QN/\mathbb Q0$ be its contracted algebra. Suppose $\dim_{\mathbb Q}A\leq4$. For every finite-dimensional right module $W$ and left module $V$, nonzero $\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)$ implies nonzero $\operatorname{Tor}_n^A(W,V)$ in arbitrarily high degrees.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: If a finite monoid $M$ has a rectangular-band minimal ideal $K$, $BM$ has finite-dimensional homotopy type, and $H_4(BM;\mathbb Q)\ne0$, then $|M\setminus K|\geq5$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Complete exclusions through order sixteen: Neither $\mathbb CP^2$ nor $S^2\times S^2$ is the classifying space of a finite monoid of order at most sixteen. Thus their minimum orders are at least seventeen. The sole census-completeness input is the bounded-quotient source of \cite{SweeneyEnumeration2026B}, in the precise families below.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Independent lower bounds of nineteen: Every finite monoid whose classifying space is $\mathbb CP^2$ or $S^2\times S^2$ has at least nineteen elements. This lower bound uses the explicit rational action-hull certificates and does not depend on an external multiplication-table census.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Independent lower bounds of twenty: Every finite monoid whose classifying space is $\mathbb CP^2$ or $S^2\times S^2$ has at least twenty elements. This bound is independent of an external monoid census.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional local algebra over a field $k$, with $A/\operatorname{rad}A=k$. Let $U$ be a finite-dimensional left $A$-module, and put \[ a=\dim_k(U/JU),\qquad b=\dim_k JU, \qquad J=\operatorname{rad}A. \] If $a>b$ and $W$ is a finite-dimensional right $A$-module satisfying $\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(W,U)=0$ for all sufficiently large $i$, then $W$ is projective. The same assertion holds with left and right interchanged.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ be a finite monoid whose minimal ideal $K$ is a rectangular band. If $A=\mathbb Q M/\mathbb Q K$ is local and $\dim_{\mathbb Q}H^2(BM;\mathbb Q)=1$, then every rational degree-two class has square zero. In particular $BM$ is not homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb{CP}^2$. This assertion has no bound on the order of $M$ and does not require finite homotopy type.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $A$ be a five-dimensional local $k$-algebra with residue field $k$. There are no right and left modules $W,V$, both of dimension three, for which \[ \dim_k\operatorname{Tor}^A_i(W,V)= \begin{cases}2&i=0,\\1&i=2,\\0&i=1\text{ or }i\geq3.\end{cases} \] More generally, it suffices to assume the displayed dimensions for $0\leq i\leq3$ and eventual vanishing of the higher Tor groups.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: For a finite monoid whose minimal ideal is a $4\times4$ rectangular band and which has five elements outside that ideal, the two augmentation modules in the band Tor formula both have dimension three. Proposition~\ref{B:local-three-by-three-product} therefore excludes a local contracted quotient for a classifying space with the rational homology of $S^2\times S^2$. The proposition makes no corresponding assertion for the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ profile: in that case the same rank equations are $2,1,1,2$, which do not by themselves give a contradiction.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $A$ be a local rational algebra of dimension five or six, and let $W,V$ be right and left modules of dimensions five and two. Suppose \[ \dim_{\mathbb Q}(W\otimes_A V)=2,\qquad \dim_{\mathbb Q}\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)=1, \] and the higher Tor groups eventually vanish. Then every balanced bilinear form on $W\times V$ factors through a fixed one-dimensional quotient of $V$ and has rank at most one. The analogous statement holds with left and right interchanged.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A finite monoid with a $3\times6$ or $6\times3$ rectangular-band minimal ideal and a local contracted rational quotient of dimension five or six cannot have classifying space homotopy equivalent to $S^2\times S^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Rational third homology in the remaining bounded images: In the six allowed hulls of Lemma~\ref{C:six-rank-two-bounded-hulls}, every closed image of order at most twenty-two and rational degree-two rank two has one of the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item its fourth rational homology is zero; \item its third rational homology is nonzero; \item it is one of the eight order-twenty images in Lemma~\ref{B:eight-rank-two-image-inflations}. \end{enumerate}
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Rank two under rational boundedness and local nullity: Let $M$ be a finite monoid with at most twenty-two elements. Assume that \[ \dim_{\mathbb Q}H_2(BM;\mathbb Q)=2,\qquad H_3(BM;\mathbb Q)=H_5(BM;\mathbb Q)=0, \] and that $H_n(BM;\mathbb Q)=0$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Assume also that every integral degree-two class on $BM$ restricts to zero on every local finite subgroup of $M$. Then every product of two rational degree-two classes is zero. No condition on mod-two homology or integral second-homology torsion is required.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: If $|M|\leq22$, $BM$ has finite CW homotopy type, $\dim_{\mathbb Q}H_2(BM;\mathbb Q)=2$, and $H_3(BM;\mathbb Q)=H_5(BM;\mathbb Q)=0$, then every rational degree-two product on $BM$ is zero.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The theorem also applies when a map $BM\to X$ to a finite CW complex induces a surjection on integral second cohomology, provided the displayed rational homology hypotheses hold. Indeed each integral class then pulls back from $X$, and Miller's theorem kills its restriction to every local finite group. This formulation asserts neither finite CW type of $BM$ nor a result for second-homology rank greater than two.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: All small sources over the eight rank-two images: Let $M$ have a $4\times4$ rectangular-band minimal ideal and at most twenty-two elements. Suppose its faithful row-and-column action image is, up to relabeling or opposition, one of the eight order-twenty images in Lemma~\ref{C:six-rank-two-bounded-hulls}. Then \[ H_3(BM;\mathbb Q)\ne0 \quad\hbox{or}\quad H_5(BM;\mathbb Q)\ne0. \]
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The bounded rank-two obstruction: Let $M$ be a finite monoid of order at most twenty-two, and suppose $BM$ has finite CW homotopy type. Assume \[ \begin{gathered} \dim_{\mathbb Q}H_2(BM;\mathbb Q)=2,\qquad \dim_{\mathbb F_2}H_2(BM;\mathbb F_2)=2, \\ H_3(BM;\mathbb F_2)=0,\qquad H_5(BM;\mathbb Q)=0. \end{gathered} \] Then every product of two rational degree-two classes is zero. In particular, the same conclusion holds under the simpler integral hypotheses \[ H_2(BM;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^2,\qquad H_3(BM;\mathbb Z)=0,\qquad H_5(BM;\mathbb Q)=0. \]
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: No finite monoid with at most twenty-two elements has classifying space homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb CP^2\vee S^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The theorem does not assert a result for higher second-homology ranks or for arbitrary sources over a small image. In particular the unbounded homology of an image was never substituted for a source obstruction: the finite third/fifth-homology calculations are performed on every actual source through the stated bound. For a $4\times4$ band, extending the source order from twenty-two through twenty-five introduces precisely the three new outside sizes $q=7,8,9$. It requires new faithful images as well as larger fibres over the eight images considered here.

statement: Let $M$ be a finite monoid with a $4\times4$ minimal band and $BM\simeq\CP^2$. Its transformation image is contained, after relabeling the rows and columns, in one of the three hulls numbered $216$, $217$, and $221$ in the complete classification below. The statement does not assume that this image, or its ambient hull, has finite-dimensional classifying space.

statement: A finite monoid of type $S^2\times S^2$ cannot have a minimal ideal with three rows and five columns, or the opposite shape, regardless of its minimal maximal group. Among finite monoids of type $\CP^2$ with that shape, the minimum order is twenty-three, attained by Theorem~\ref{B:CP23}.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A finite model with square two: There is a $23$-element monoid with classifying space $S^2\cup_{2\eta}e^4$, where $\eta$ generates $\pi_3(S^2)$. Its minimal ideal is a three-by-four rectangular band.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Three-by-four target obstructions: A finite monoid with a three-by-four rectangular minimal band cannot have classifying space $\mathbb CP^2$. A finite monoid whose minimal ideal has three rows and four columns, with any maximal group, cannot have classifying space $S^2\times S^2$. Both assertions also hold after interchanging rows and columns.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Rank-one balanced forms: Let the minimal ideal of a finite monoid be a rectangular band. A rational degree-two class whose balanced matrix has rank at most one has square zero. No finite-homotopy hypothesis is needed.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The finite-type three-by-three obstruction: Let $M$ be a finite monoid whose minimal ideal has three rows and three columns, with any finite maximal group. If $BM$ has finite CW homotopy type, then every product \[ H^2(BM;\mathbb Q)\otimes H^2(BM;\mathbb Q) \longrightarrow H^4(BM;\mathbb Q) \] is zero. In particular, $BM$ is neither $\mathbb CP^2$ nor $S^2\times S^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The last proof also applies when a homomorphism from the original finite monoid has an action image containing a three-by-three band, and the degree-two classes under consideration factor through that image. The finite-CW hypothesis is imposed on the original monoid: its local groups supply the same forbidden-character obstruction. This relative form permits quotienting duplicate row or column values in a balanced-form computation.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $A$ be either the five-dimensional Nakayama algebra of Lemma~\ref{B:five-exceptional-targets} times $\mathbb Q$, or the six-dimensional algebra with vertex idempotents $e,f$, radical basis $x,a,b,c$, and \[ x\in eAe,\quad a\in eAf,\quad b\in fAe,\quad c\in eAe, \qquad x^2=ab=c, \] all other products of radical basis elements being zero. Let $V$ be the two-dimensional left module on which $b$ is the nonzero cross-arrow and all other radical elements act by zero. In the direct-product case the isolated rational factor acts by zero. Suppose a five-dimensional right module $W$ satisfies \[ (\dim\operatorname{Tor}_0^A(W,V), \dim\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(W,V), \dim\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V))=(2,0,1). \] Then $W$ and $V$ have the same annihilator, and are faithful over the quotient by that annihilator, which is the path algebra of one arrow. In the Nakayama product case the annihilator is $(a,c)\oplus\mathbb Q$; in the six-dimensional case it is $(x,a,c)$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: None of the $124$ finite-projective-dimension triangular row modules retained by the six-dimensional quotient census can occur in a monoid with a $3\times6$ rectangular-band minimal ideal and classifying space $S^2\times S^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $A$ be a rational algebra of dimension six and let $V$ be a two-dimensional module whose action algebra is the full triangular two-by-two rational matrix algebra. If $A/\operatorname{rad}A$ is not a product of copies of $\mathbb Q$, then eventual vanishing of $\operatorname{Tor}^A_n(W,V)$ implies $\operatorname{Tor}^A_2(W,V)=0$ for every finite-dimensional right module $W$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: An odd Euler characteristic at a local corner: Let $B$ be a four-dimensional local rational algebra with residue field $k=\mathbb Q$, and put \[ A=\begin{pmatrix}k&k\\0&B\end{pmatrix}, \] where the right $B$-action on the displayed cross bimodule is its residue character. Let $V$ be the two-dimensional left module with one copy of $k$ at each vertex and with the cross-arrow acting as the identity. For every five-dimensional right $A$-module $W$, the groups $\operatorname{Tor}^A_n(W,V)$ are nonzero in arbitrarily high degrees.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: For the opposite triangular orientation $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}B&k\\0&k\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, the two-dimensional nonsplit cross-arrow module is itself the projective at the $k$-vertex. Its higher Tor groups are zero. Thus the two orientations of a local four-dimensional corner with a single radical-annihilated cross-arrow cannot produce Tor dimensions $2,0,1,0,\ldots$ with augmentation dimensions $(\dim W,\dim V)=(5,2)$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $A$ be one of the following radical-square-zero rational algebras, with orthogonal primitive idempotents $e_1,e_2,e_3$. Suppose $\dim W=5$, $\dim V=2$, and \[ \bigl(\dim\operatorname{Tor}_0^A(W,V), \dim\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(W,V), \dim\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)\bigr)=(2,0,1). \] The conclusions below concern every such module pair, without assuming that the displayed algebra basis is a monoid basis. \begin{enumerate} \item For the triangle algebra, take $a\in e_1Ae_2$, $b\in e_2Ae_3$, $c\in e_1Ae_3$ and let $V$ be the two-dimensional module on which $c$ is the nonzero arrow. Either every balanced form has rank at most one, or $W$ is faithful over $A/(a)$ or over $A/(b)$. In the first faithful case the vertex dimensions of $W$ are $(1,1,3)$; in the second they are $(2,1,2)$. \item For the parallel-chain algebra, take $a\in e_1Ae_2$ and $b,c\in e_2Ae_3$, with $b,c$ independent. Let $V$ have $b$ acting as the identity between its one-dimensional vertex spaces and $c$ acting as zero. Either every balanced form has rank at most one, or $W$ is faithful over $A/(a)$, with vertex dimensions $(1,1,3)$. \end{enumerate} Every quotient algebra appearing in the faithful alternatives is hereditary, as is each of its further algebra quotients.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The literal arrow-ideal gate: Among the $458$ actual row-module cases in the two square-zero exceptions of Proposition~\ref{B:six-row-census}, the faithful alternatives of Lemma~\ref{B:six-squarezero-target-modules} give $636$ one-dimensional arrow ideals to test. All $280$ parallel-chain ideals and $348$ of the $356$ triangle ideals are killed by the faithful transformation-pair image of every monoid realizing the corresponding module pair. Their images therefore have zero rational fourth homology and all degree-two products in the original monoids are zero. The only eight exceptions to this literal-ideal test have the source indices and ideals listed in the next proposition.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The eight remaining affine triangle families: None of the eight remaining faithful triangle cases in Lemma~\ref{B:six-squarezero-literal-ideals} can give the cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The $458$ square-zero row-module exceptions in Proposition~\ref{B:six-row-census} cannot occur for a twenty-four-element monoid model of $S^2\times S^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Three-dimensional quotient algebras: Let $A$ be a unital finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q$-algebra with $\dim_{\mathbb Q}A\leq3$, let $W$ be a finite-dimensional right $A$-module, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional left $A$-module. If $\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)\ne0$, then \[ \operatorname{Tor}_n^A(W,V)\ne0\qquad\text{for every }n\geq2. \] Consequently, if these Tor groups vanish in all sufficiently high degrees, then $\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)=0$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ be a finite monoid whose minimal ideal $K$ is a rectangular band. If $BM$ has finite-dimensional homotopy type and $H_4(BM;\mathbb Q)\ne0$, then $|M\setminus K|\geq4$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Three-by-five obstruction with explicit source hypotheses: Let $M$ be a finite monoid of order at most twenty-two with a three-by-five rectangular minimal band, or the opposite shape. Suppose that \[ H_*(BM;\Q)\cong H_*(\CP^2;\Q) \] as graded vector spaces, and that every integral degree-two class on $BM$ restricts to zero along every map $BG\to BM$ from a finite group. Then the square of a generator of $H^2(BM;\Z)\cong\Z$ is not primitive in $H^4(BM;\Z)/\operatorname{torsion}$. In particular the three-by-five lower-bound obstruction applies under these hypotheses without assuming that $BM$ has finite CW type.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The assumption on rational homology explicitly includes $H_3(BM;\Q)=0$; bounded rational homology together with one-dimensional $H^2$ and $H^4$ alone is not being substituted for it. Only the restrictions to the eventual local groups appearing in the cited hull certificates are needed. The stronger all-finite-group formulation above is convenient when those restrictions are supplied by a map to a finite simply connected target. The proposition concerns band sources. For order at most twenty-two a three-by-five minimal ideal with a nontrivial maximal group is impossible, since that ideal alone would have at least thirty elements.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: In the two exceptional algebras of Proposition~\ref{B:five-nonlocal-exceptions}, suppose \[ \dim V=2,\quad\dim W=5,\qquad (\dim\operatorname{Tor}_0, \dim\operatorname{Tor}_1, \dim\operatorname{Tor}_2)=(2,0,1). \] For the zero-composite line algebra the only pair is \[ V=S_1\oplus S_3,\qquad W=T_1\oplus e_1A\oplus e_2A. \] Every balanced form for this pair factors through the same one-dimensional quotient $S_1$ of $V$. For the Nakayama algebra the only pair is \[ V=L=Ae_1/\mathbb Qc,\qquad W=T_2\oplus(e_2A)^{\oplus2}. \] Both modules of this latter pair are faithful over $A/I$, where $I=\operatorname{span}(a,c)$, and $A/I$ is the path algebra of one arrow.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The actual Nakayama multiplicative bases: Suppose a contracted finite-monoid algebra of dimension five is isomorphic to the Nakayama algebra in Lemma~\ref{B:five-two-by-five-pairs}. In its distinguished monoid basis, the ideal $I=\operatorname{span}(a,c)$ is spanned by basis vectors lying in $I$ and differences of two basis vectors that have the same image in $A/I$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A finite monoid with a $3\times6$ or $6\times3$ rectangular-band minimal ideal and exactly five elements outside that ideal cannot have classifying space homotopy equivalent to $S^2\times S^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The Nakayama balanced forms themselves have rank two. On one $e_2A$ summand, in the bases $(e_2,b)$ and $(\bar e_1,\bar b)$, the multiplication pairing is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The proof uses the actual multiplicative-basis quotient and does not infer rank-one factorization from $e_2A\otimes_A L\cong e_2L$. As a separate construction check, \path{code/d_product23_nakayama.py} enumerates all $732$ affine lifts for the standard zero basis: four row-action types and $183$ column-action types. Every resulting twenty-three-element monoid has the required finite additive homology, but all $2\times2$ cup matrices are zero. This last family calculation is not used in the exhaustive multiplicative-basis argument above.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Finite targets kill the torsion from a group above a band: Let $H$ be a finite group acting on finite nonempty row and column sets $I,J$, and let $S=H\amalg(I\times J)$ be the corresponding group-band monoid. Every map $BS\to X$ to a connected finite CW complex kills the torsion subgroup of $H_2(BS;\Z)$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A three-by-three minimal band has no three-primary torsion: Let $M$ be a finite monoid whose minimal ideal is a $3\times3$ rectangular band. If $BM$ has finite CW homotopy type, then $H_2(BM;\Z)$ has no nonzero three-primary torsion.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let a finite monoid act on a three-element set, and suppose the algebra generated on its rational augmentation module is the full triangular two-by-two matrix algebra. After relabeling the set as $\{0,1,2\}$, every acting transformation $s$ satisfies \[ s(0)=s(1)\quad\hbox{or}\quad\{s(0),s(1)\}=\{0,1\}. \] Collapsing the three constant maps gives a thirteen-element monoid $S_{13}$. The induced augmentation representation factors through this monoid. The only remaining relabeling that preserves the unique invariant line is the transposition of $0$ and $1$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional algebra, $V$ a left module, and let $K$ be a first syzygy of $V$ after removal of projective direct summands. Suppose that for some $d\geq1$, $K$ is a direct summand of a $d$th syzygy of $K$, up to projective direct summands. If $\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)\ne0$, then $\operatorname{Tor}_n^A(W,V)\ne0$ for arbitrarily large $n$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Complete six-dimensional triangular-row reduction: Let $A$ be a six-dimensional contracted finite-monoid algebra over $\mathbb Q$. Let $V$ be the two-dimensional augmentation module of an action on three points, with full triangular action algebra, and let $\dim W=5$. Suppose \[ (\dim\operatorname{Tor}_0^A(W,V), \dim\operatorname{Tor}_1^A(W,V), \dim\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V))=(2,0,1) \] and the Tor groups vanish in all sufficiently large degrees. Up to isomorphism of the actual contracted monoid and rational isomorphism of $V$, the pair $(A,V)$ belongs to one of the following two explicitly enumerated lists: \[ \begin{array}{c|r} \text{type}&\text{row-module records}\\\hline J^2=0,\ \text{two parallel arrows followed by one arrow}&280\\ J^2=0,\ \text{oriented triangle with zero length-two products}&178\\ \text{Nakayama algebra of dimension five times }\mathbb Q&104\\ x^2=ab=c\text{ with the thin }b\text{-module}&20. \end{array} \] Here the first two entries have three vertices and three arrows; in the oriented triangle one arrow is the direct bypass of the other two. The last two entries are those of Lemma~\ref{B:six-pd2-row-pairs}.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Suppose the minimal ideal of a finite monoid is a rectangular band with three rows. If two rational degree-two classes have rank-one balanced matrices, their product is zero. The same statement holds with rows and columns interchanged. No finiteness assumption on the homotopy type is required.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ have a three-row rectangular-band minimal ideal, and let $V$ be its two-dimensional rational row augmentation module. If $V$ is a direct sum of one-dimensional modules, every product of two rational degree-two classes of $BM$ is zero.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $A$ be a rational algebra of dimension at most six, and let $V$ be a simple left $A$-module of rational dimension two. For every right module $W$, either $V$ is projective or $\dim_{\mathbb Q}\operatorname{Tor}^A_n(W,V)$ is even for every $n$. In particular, a one-dimensional degree-two Tor group cannot occur.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: For a possible twenty-four-element monoid model of $S^2\times S^2$ whose minimal ideal is a $3\times6$ band, the two-dimensional row augmentation module over the six-dimensional contracted rational algebra must be indecomposable and nonsemisimple. Its image algebra in $\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q}(V)$ is either $\mathbb Q[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ or the algebra of upper triangular two-by-two rational matrices.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Suppose the minimal ideal of a finite monoid $M$ is a rectangular band with three rows, and its rational row augmentation module $V$ has image algebra $\mathbb Q[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ acting nonsemisimply. Then either all products of rational degree-two classes vanish, or their cup-product pairing has a nonzero common radical. Consequently $BM$ cannot have the cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$. If $\dim H^2(BM;\mathbb Q)=1$, its generator has square zero as well.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: In the situation of Corollary~\ref{B:three-by-six-order24-row-reduction}, the row augmentation image is the full triangular two-by-two rational matrix algebra. Thus the possible twenty-four-element product case has a nonsplit extension of two distinct rational characters as its row augmentation module.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Two rows permit only elementary two-torsion: Let $M$ be a finite monoid whose minimal ideal is a rectangular band with two rows or two columns. If $BM$ has finite CW homotopy type, then the torsion subgroup of $H_2(BM;\mathbb Z)$ is a direct sum of copies of $\mathbb Z/2$. In particular it has no odd-primary torsion and no element of order four. If every row action fixes the two rows or is constant, then $H_2(BM;\mathbb Z)$ is torsion-free.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: On a set of $n$ labelled elements with identity fixed at $0$, the numbers of monoid structures for $1\le n\le7$ are \[ 1,\ 2,\ 11,\ 156,\ 4122,\ 208672,\ 18507440. \] For $n\le6$ the numbers up to isomorphism and opposite are $1,2,6,27,156,1373$. Every integral $(H_1,H_2,H_3)$ multiplicity in \texttt{OWN\_RESULTS.md}, Statement 6.1(a)--(c), is reproduced. The connected category counts, with object identities labelled and nonidentity arrows sorted by source and target, are as follows. \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{rrrrr}\toprule Arrows & 2 objects & 3 objects & 4 objects & 5 objects\\\midrule 3&2&0&0&0\\ 4&11&0&0&0\\ 5&76&6&0&0\\ 6&977&54&0&0\\ 7&22798&498&32&0\\ 8&1016844&6324&406&0\\ 9&\text{not enumerated}&133543&4468&250\\\bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{center} All connected categories with at most seven arrows are covered. The additional eight- and nine-arrow counts have only the scopes displayed; the two-object nine-arrow cell is not claimed. Cases with $N<2k-1$ are zero because a connected graph on $k$ objects needs at least $k-1$ nonidentity arrows.

statement: Up to isomorphism, exactly one category with three objects and nine arrows has classifying space of type $\RP^2$. It is $R_2$: the objects are $0,1,2$, each $\operatorname{Hom}(i,j)$ for $i<j$ is $C_2$, all endomorphisms are identities, and composition is addition in $C_2$. Its classifying space is homeomorphic to $\RP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: There are exactly four isomorphism classes of categories with seven arrows and classifying space of type $S^3$. All are monoids. They are $P,P^{\op}$, $Q,Q^{\op}$, where $P$ and $Q$ have the following tables, with $0$ the identity: \[ P=\begin{pmatrix} 0&1&2&3&4&5&6\\ 1&1&1&3&3&1&1\\ 2&2&2&4&4&2&2\\ 3&1&1&3&3&1&1\\ 4&2&2&4&4&2&2\\ 5&1&2&3&4&5&5\\ 6&1&2&3&4&6&6 \end{pmatrix},\qquad Q=\begin{pmatrix} 0&1&2&3&4&5&6\\ 1&2&2&2&4&4&1\\ 2&2&2&2&4&4&2\\ 3&3&3&3&5&5&3\\ 4&2&2&2&4&4&2\\ 5&3&3&3&5&5&3\\ 6&2&2&3&4&5&6 \end{pmatrix}. \]
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A torsion-support estimate: Let $K$ be a finite simplicial complex and suppose $H_1(K;\Z)$ has nonzero $p$-torsion for a prime $p$. There is a connected two-dimensional subcomplex $L$ with $v$ vertices and $e$ edges such that $e\ge3v-3$, and the induced full subcomplex on these vertices still has $p$-torsion in $H_1$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The least number of arrows, including identities, of a finite poset with classifying space of type $\RP^2$ is exactly $49$. More generally every finite poset whose first integral homology has torsion has at least $49$ arrows.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The least number of arrows of a category of type $S^1\vee S^1$ is five.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Two-object cup-product reductions: Let $C$ be a finite category with two objects and endomorphism monoids $M,N$. Suppose first that all cross arrows go in one direction, and write $S$ for that nonempty cross-biset. \begin{enumerate} \item If $|S|=1$, every positive-degree integral cohomology product of $BC$ vanishes. \item If $|S|=2$ and one of $BM,BN$ is contractible, every product of two positive-degree integral classes of $BC$ is annihilated by two. If that vertex space is only rationally acyclic, every such rational product vanishes. \item If both $BM$ and $BN$ are rationally acyclic, every positive-degree rational product of $BC$ vanishes, for arbitrary $S$. \end{enumerate} If arrows instead go in both directions and one endomorphism monoid is trivial, $BC$ is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of the other endomorphism monoid. If each of the two cross-hom sets has one element, $BC$ is contractible.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Small vertex monoids in a triangular category: No triangular two-object category with at most ten arrows has classifying space $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Three-object star reductions: Suppose a three-object category has cross arrows only on two legs of a star, both pointing toward its center or both pointing away from it. If both cross-hom sets are singletons, all positive cohomology products vanish. If one leg is a singleton with a trivial endomorphism monoid at its leaf, and the other leaf has rationally acyclic classifying space, all positive rational products vanish.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Triangular categories with eleven arrows: No triangular two-object category with at most eleven arrows has classifying space $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: No $\mathbb CP^2$ category with at most eleven arrows: Every finite category whose classifying space has the homotopy type of $\mathbb CP^2$ has at least twelve arrows.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

Its complete composition table and its comparison with the twenty-three-element monoid in Theorem~\ref{B:CP23} are given in \path{code/outputs/a_CP22_category.json}.

statement: An all-order obstruction to literal small-target Hopf maps: Let $M$ be a finite monoid with $H_2(BM;\Q)=0$. Every unital homomorphism $M\to L_0$ induces a nullhomotopic map of classifying spaces. In particular no such homomorphism from a finite monoid of type $S^3$ represents a Hopf map to the five-element model of $S^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Scope of subsequent reductions: The program \texttt{c\_CP40\_all\_congruences.py} enumerates the complete lattice of 28\,135 congruences of the forty-arrow table that preserve its two objects and hom-set types. Among the proper quotients, 25\,704 have zero rational degree-two homology at the endomorphism-monoid vertex, which forces the degree-two square of the act cone to vanish; the other 2430 have zero degree-two homology over $\mathbb F_2$. Thus no proper quotient in this specified sense is another $\mathbb CP^2$ model. There are ten maximal proper wide subcategories of this table. Their complete act-cone projective resolutions, reconstructed and checked independently, all have different additive homology from $\mathbb CP^2$. This does not exclude more deeply nested subcategories. A separate search of all sixteen smaller full subcategories retaining the cone object and at least one of its proper Karoubi-object classes finds either the wrong second Betti number or a zero degree-two square. These are explicitly scoped reduction checks, not a proof that forty is the category minimum. The records are \path{code/outputs/c_CP40_all_congruences.json}, \path{code/outputs/d_cp2_subcategory_search.json}, and \path{code/outputs/d_cp2_karoubi_search.json}.
