statement: One core orbit for the five-element sphere corner: Let $P=\{1\}\sqcup(\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\})$ be the five-element sphere monoid, with minimal band $K$, and let $S$ be a finite nonempty $(P,N)$-biset. Suppose that $KS$ is one two-point left $K$-orbit and that $P$ has no fixed state in $S$. If the collage $X$ has \[ \dim H^2(X;\mathbb Q)=1,\qquad H_3(X;\mathbb Q)=0, \] its degree-two generator has square zero. In particular $X$ cannot have type $\mathbb{CP}^2$. There is no bound on $|S|$ or $|N|$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Four states opposite the sphere corner: Let $S$ be a nonempty $(P,N)$-biset with $|S|\leq4$. If $H^2(BN;\mathbb Q)=0$, its collage cannot have type $\mathbb{CP}^2$. When the left $P$-action has no fixed state, the same conclusion holds without that cohomological hypothesis on $N$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The sixteen-arrow profile $(5,7,4)$ needs no separate enumeration. If its seven-element vertex has zero rational degree-two cohomology, apply Proposition~\ref{C:P5-four-state-bisets}; otherwise its opposite is in the complete $(7,5,4)$ catalog. Any already computed $(5,7,4)$ records are independent controls and need not be a premise of the exclusion.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The literal two-step trivial-module resolution: Let $P=\{1\}\sqcup\{x_{ij}:i,j\in\{0,1\}\}$, where $x_{ij}x_{kl}=x_{il}$, and let $A=\Q P$. Put \[ e=x_{00},\qquad f=1-e,\qquad a=x_{10}-x_{00},\qquad b=x_{01}-x_{00}. \] The trivial left $A$-module has the exact projective resolution \[ 0\longrightarrow Ae\xrightarrow{\ {-}\,b\ }Af \xrightarrow{\ {-}\,a\ }Ae \xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon\ }\Q\longrightarrow0. \] For every right $A$-module $W$ this identifies \[ \operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,\Q) =\ker\bigl(We\xrightarrow{\ {-}\,b\ }Wf\bigr). \]
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A universal graph obstruction over $P_5$: Let $P$ be the five-element monoid of the preceding lemma, and let it act on the right of a nonempty finite graph $\Gamma$. Each actor is required to send vertices to vertices and each oriented edge at unit speed to an oriented edge or to collapse it to a vertex. Write \[ X=\operatorname{hocofib}(\Gamma_{hP}\longrightarrow BP). \] Then either the action has a common fixed vertex, or $H_4(X;\Q)=0$. In either case all products of two rational degree-two classes on $X$ vanish. No connectedness or finite-CW-type hypothesis is imposed on $X$ or $\Gamma_{hP}$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The $P_5$--right-zero-three collage: Let $R=\{1,p,q\}$ be the identity-adjoined two-element right-zero band. For every finite $(R,P)$-biset $S$, the two-object collage has zero rational degree-two products. In particular it cannot have type $\CP^2$, at any number of states. The opposite collage is excluded as well.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A common fixed row for nonconstant column actors: Let $M$ have rectangular-band minimal ideal $I\times\{0,1\}$. Write $\sigma_m:I\to I$ and $\tau_m:\{0,1\}\to\{0,1\}$ for its row and column actions. Suppose there is a row $i_0$ fixed by every $\sigma_m$ for which $\tau_m$ is nonconstant. Then for every nonempty finite right $M$-set $S$, all products \[ H^2(B\mathcal C(M,S);\mathbb Z)\otimes H^2(B\mathcal C(M,S);\mathbb Z) \longrightarrow H^4(B\mathcal C(M,S);\mathbb Z) \] are zero. In particular no such act cone is a projective plane. There is no bound on the number of rows, states, or outside elements, and no finiteness hypothesis on the classifying space.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: All dual-number three-row act cones: Suppose $M$ has a $3\times2$ rectangular-band minimal ideal and the image of its rational row augmentation representation is the nonsemisimple dual-number algebra. For every finite right $M$-set $S$, all integral degree-two products on $B\mathcal C(M,S)$ are zero. In particular no such cone realizes $\mathbb CP^2$, regardless of the sizes of $M$ and $S$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A completed finite control and a superseded search: Before the preceding primitive was found, a bounded upper-model search was completed for one explicit six-dimensional contracted basis: a square-zero loop at the first vertex of a zero-composite three-vertex chain. Its $72$ literal $3\times2$ affine lifts and $144$ trace/rank cases gave $593536$ eight-state acts after the trace constraints. Of these, $275040$ had the required exact Tor profile, and $90240$ retained a possible rank-two balanced class. The $10236$ state-orbit representatives all had zero mod-two square, with actual stored primitives checked on $258858204$ four-simplices. The code and outputs have prefix \path{a_dual_loop_chain}. This finite control is not used in the all-order proof. The broader restricted order-twelve dual-row target stream \path{code/outputs/a_twelve_dual_targets.tsv} was intentionally interrupted when the all-order theorem superseded it. It is retained as an incomplete research prefix, not a complete census and not a premise of any exclusion.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The literal act-cone kernel: Let $M$ be a monoid, $S$ a nonempty right $M$-set, $k$ a field, $R=kM$, and $L=\ker(kS\to k)$. Write $C(M,S)$ for the two-object act category. The kernel of the normalized-chain map \[ C_*(BC(M,S);k)\longrightarrow C_*(BC(M,*);k) \] is naturally the suspension of the normalized two-sided bar $B_*(L,R,k)$. In degree $n+1$ the comparison sends \[ w[a_1|\cdots|a_n]\longmapsto (-1)^{n(n-1)/2}\sum_{s\in S}w_s [a_n|\cdots|a_1|s],\qquad w=\sum_s w_s s. \] Consequently it induces $\operatorname{Tor}_n^R(L,k)\cong\widetilde H_{n+1}(BC(M,S);k)$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A projective comparison for the affine square: Suppose $M$ has minimal band $I\times J$ acting constantly on $S$. Choose base elements $i_0\in I$ and $s_0\in S$ as in the constant-action compression, and put $V=\widetilde{kI}$ and $W=\widetilde{kS}=L$. Let $F:W\times V\to k$ be a balanced bilinear form and let $u_F$ be its affine degree-two class on $C(M,S)$. Set \[ \alpha_a=e_{\sigma_a(i_0)}-e_{i_0},\qquad \beta_b=e_{s_0b}-e_{s_0}. \] On the two-sided bar of Lemma~\ref{C:act-cone-literal-bar-kernel}, the pullback of $u_F^2$ in degree three is, up to the one common minus sign supplied by that lemma, \[ w[a|b|c]\longmapsto F(w,\alpha_a)F(\beta_b,\alpha_c). \] Let $P_\bullet\to k$ be a projective resolution of the trivial left $R$-module, with each displayed summand a literal ideal $R\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon^2=\varepsilon$. Projective terms $P_0,\ldots,P_3$ with exactness through $P_2$ (so $P_3$ surjects onto $\ker d_2$), together with their comparison to the normalized free left bar resolution, suffice to certify that this square is a coboundary by exhibiting a primitive on $L\otimes_RP_\bullet$. No termination of the undisplayed resolution is required.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: What a finite-field square certificate proves: In the application over $\mathbb F_{65521}$, the exact contracted projective prefix gives $\dim\operatorname{Tor}_0^{kM/kK}(W,V)=1$. A nonzero balanced form is therefore the nonzero degree-two cohomology class, by the affine representative and compression comparison. A primitive from the preceding proposition proves that this actual field class has square zero and excludes $\mathbb CP^2$. It does not infer rational rank from a modular rank, nor infer vanishing of higher homology from a finite prefix. The routines are \path{code/a_monoid_bar_prefix_modp.py} and \path{code/a_act_bar_square_modp.py}; all projective ideals, full embedded kernels, idempotent supports and sparse comparison chain equations are retained explicitly.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The rank-one form of the small-corner lemma: Let a finite category $S$ be the source block of a collage whose sink corner $N$ has at most four elements. Suppose every cross stalk is nonempty and has at most two elements. If the collage has rational second-cohomology dimension at most one, its degree-two square vanishes. The opposite statement holds for a small source corner.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Two parallel-arrow excesses with small corners: Let $C$ be a connected finite category with acyclic support, all corner orders at most four, support cycle rank at most six, and total parallel-arrow excess at most two. If $\dim H^2(BC;\mathbb Q)\leq1$, its square vanishes.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $C$ have $k$ objects, $n$ arrows, and acyclic support. If $n\leq2k+7$, then $BC\not\simeq\mathbb CP^2$. In particular every acyclic seven-object category with at most twenty-one arrows is excluded.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Two support-homology budgets: Let $\Pi$ be a finite connected poset and let $R$ be the cycle rank of its undirected comparability graph. If $R\leq6$, then $H_2(B\Pi;\mathbb Q)=0$. If $R\leq8$, then $H_4(B\Pi;\mathbb Q)=0$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A cut through the parallel hom-sets: Let $C$ be a finite category with acyclic support of cycle rank at most six. Suppose every corner has zero rational second cohomology. Call a nonempty cross hom-set parallel if it has at least two arrows. Suppose no two parallel hom-sets $C(x,y)$ and $C(z,w)$ satisfy $y\leq z$ in the support order. Then every product of two rational degree-two classes on $BC$ vanishes.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $C$ have $k$ objects, $n$ arrows, and acyclic support. If $n\leq2k+6$, then $BC\not\simeq\mathbb CP^2$. In particular the acyclic seven-object case is excluded through twenty arrows.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Singleton hom-sets and the support poset: Let $C$ be a finite connected category with at least two objects, acyclic support, and exactly one arrow in each nonempty hom-set between distinct objects. Let $\Pi$ be its support poset. The actual functor $q:C\to\Pi$ which collapses every corner monoid to its identity induces an isomorphism \[ q^*:H^2(B\Pi;\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ } H^2(BC;\mathbb Q). \] No assumption on the positive rational homology of the corner monoids is required.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Small cycle rank of a support graph: Let $\Pi$ be a finite connected poset, let $G$ be its undirected comparability graph, and put $R=|E(G)|-|V(G)|+1$. If $R\leq6$, then $H_4(B\Pi;\mathbb Q)=0$. If $R\leq3$ and $H_1(B\Pi;\mathbb F_2)=0$, then $G$ is chordal. In the latter case its maximal-clique decomposition has the following possibilities after bridges and cut vertices are separated: \begin{itemize} \item at $R=1$, a single triangle; \item at $R=2$, triangles or two triangles sharing an edge; \item at $R=3$, at most three triangles glued along edges or vertices in a clique tree, or one complete four-vertex block. \end{itemize} The classifying-space nerve of a category with this support is the corresponding union of its full clique subcategory nerves, with their actual full intersection subcategories.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $C$ be a finite category with $k$ objects, $n$ arrows, and acyclic support. If $n\leq2k+5$, then $BC\not\simeq\mathbb CP^2$. In particular every category with acyclic support, at least eight objects, and at most twenty-one arrows is excluded.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A right-zero action has a natural graph model: Let $R=\{1,p,q\}$, with $ab=b$ for $a,b\in\{p,q\}$, act on the left on a finite set $T$. Its two nonidentity transformations $P,Q$ are retractions onto the same subset $U\subseteq T$. The action category has a natural classifying space equivalence to the graph with vertices $U$ and, for each $t\in T\setminus U$, one oriented edge from $P(t)$ to $Q(t)$. An equivariant set map sends this edge to the edge indexed by the image of $t$, or collapses it to a vertex if that image belongs to the new common retraction image.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Two commuting right-zero actions: Suppose that $P_0,P_1$ and $Q_0,Q_1$ are two commuting pairs of retractions on a finite set $T$, each pair having a common image. Put $U=\operatorname{im}P_0=\operatorname{im}P_1$ and $V=\operatorname{im}Q_0=\operatorname{im}Q_1$. The double action correspondence has a natural finite CW model $K(T)$ with cells \[ \begin{array}{c|l} 0&U\cap V\\ 1&U\setminus V\quad\text{and}\quad V\setminus U\\ 2&T\setminus(U\cup V). \end{array} \] Its two-cell indexed by $t$ has the four faces indexed by $P_0t,P_1t,Q_0t,Q_1t$, with a face collapsed when its index lies in $U\cap V$. Equivariant maps preserve these cells or collapse a coordinate.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The two-circle chart family has zero degree-two products: Let $C$ have objects $0,1,2$ and only forward cross arrows. Let $\operatorname{End}(0)$ be the identity-adjoined two-element left-zero band, $\operatorname{End}(1)=1$, and let $\operatorname{End}(2)$ be the identity-adjoined two-element right-zero band. Thus both these corner monoids have order three. Suppose \[ C(0,1)=\{a_0,a_1\},\qquad C(1,2)=\{b_0,b_1\}, \] with every nonidentity element of the first corner sending both $a_i$ to $a_0$ by precomposition, and every nonidentity element of the last corner sending both $b_i$ to $b_0$ by postcomposition. The set $C(0,2)$ may be any finite nonempty biset, and composition may be any equivariant map. Then every rational product of degree-two classes on $BC$ is zero. In particular this family never realizes $\mathbb {CP}^2$, regardless of its total number of arrows.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The completed sixteen-arrow control: For $|T|=5$, \path{code/d_affine_chart16.py} enumerates all $1536$ ordered pairs of retractions onto a common subset. They give $24$ right-action orbits under state permutations. Restoring every relative left-action position gives $3374$ commuting bisets and $12437$ equivariant composition choices. Exactly $2311$ literal tables have $H_1(-;\mathbb F_2)=0$ and one-dimensional $H_2$. The independent bar checker verifies all $249588$ typed associativity equations and an explicit zero-square primitive for every one of these tables. The complete records have prefix \path{code/outputs/d_affine_chart16_CP2}. This calculation is a control of the universal theorem, not its proof.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Boundary values distinguish degenerate cells: For the commuting retractions in Lemma~\ref{C:two-retraction-cubical-model}, the map \[ U\cup V\longrightarrow T^4,\qquad t\longmapsto(P_0t,P_1t,Q_0t,Q_1t) \] is injective.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The two-edge-circle chart family has zero products: Keep the corner monoids and support of Theorem~\ref{C:affine-chart-family-zero}, but take the two adjacent hom-sets to be \[ A=\{u_0,u_1,a_0,a_1\},\qquad B=\{v_0,v_1,b_0,b_1\}. \] The two nonidentity precomposition maps fix both $u_\eta$ and send each $a_j$ to $u_0$ or $u_1$, respectively. The two nonidentity postcomposition maps fix both $v_\eta$ and send each $b_i$ to $v_0$ or $v_1$, respectively. Allow any finite nonempty long-edge biset $T=C(0,2)$ and any equivariant composition. Every rational product of two degree-two classes on $BC$ is zero. Thus this entire family fails to realize $\mathbb {CP}^2$ at every size.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Completed controls through twenty-one arrows: The exact generator \path{code/d_affine_four_circles.py} enumerates all commuting retraction bisets and all equivariant composition maps for $1\leq|T|\leq6$, using only actual target-state and transient-edge automorphisms to remove repetitions. The respective arrow totals and numbers of literal $H_1=0$, $\dim H_2=1$ mod-two candidates are \[ \begin{array}{c|rrrrrr} \text{arrows}&16&17&18&19&20&21\\\hline \text{candidates}&0&6&44&340&2414&19652. \end{array} \] The independent bar checker verifies a zero-square primitive for all $22456$ candidates, including $4092904$ typed associativity equations. All six generator and checker streams are complete; their prefixes are \path{code/outputs/d_affine_four_circles_1} through \path{code/outputs/d_affine_four_circles_6}. These computations corroborate the theorem and are not used in its all-size proof.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A local contracted algebra with two columns: Let $M$ have a completely simple minimal ideal with two columns, and suppose its contracted rational algebra $A=\mathbb QM/\mathbb QK$ is local. Every rational degree-two product of every finite act cone of $M$ is zero. There is no bound on the number of rows or states, and the minimal maximal group may be nontrivial.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Two quotient covectors on at most five rows: Let $M$ have a minimal ideal with at most five rows and two columns. Put $V=\widetilde{\mathbb QI}$ and let $\chi$ be its column augmentation character. If \[ \dim_{\mathbb Q}\operatorname{Hom}_A(V,\mathbb Q_\chi)\geq2, \qquad A=\mathbb QM/\mathbb QK, \] then every rational degree-two product of every finite act cone is zero. No bounded-homology assumption is needed.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Three outside elements, at every row and state count: If a finite monoid has a minimal ideal with two columns and at most three outside elements, all rational degree-two products of all its finite act cones vanish.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: All degree-two products on the two small five-chain levels: Let $D$ have five linearly ordered objects, trivial endomorphisms, and a nonempty hom-set in every forward direction. If $D$ has at most nineteen arrows, then every product of two classes in $H^2(BD;\mathbb F_2)$ is zero. No assumption on its first homology or the dimension of its second homology is required.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Acyclic support with trivial endomorphisms: Let $C$ be a finite category with trivial endomorphism monoids and acyclic support on distinct objects. If $C$ has at most twenty-one arrows, then $BC$ is not homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb {CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $C$ be a connected finite category with $k$ objects and $n$ arrows, including identities, such that \[ n\leq\min\{21,2k+7\}. \] Suppose that no object is a retract of another. If $C$ has a proper strongly connected component on two objects, then $BC\not\simeq\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Every finite category with $k$ objects and $n\leq\min\{21,2k+7\}$ arrows has classifying space not homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A category of type $\mathbb CP^2$ with seventeen arrows has at most four objects. With eighteen or nineteen arrows it has at most five objects; with twenty or twenty-one arrows it has at most six objects.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A proper biset retract preserves a hypothetical projective plane: Let $S$ be a finite $(N,M)$-biset and let $f:S\to S$ be an equivariant idempotent with nonempty image $U$. If the collage on $S$ has type $\mathbb CP^2$, then the collage on $U$ has type $\mathbb CP^2$ as well.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A least-arrow two-object triangular model of $\mathbb CP^2$ has no proper equivariant biset retraction. At sixteen arrows, every proper equivariant idempotent on the cross-biset is excluded by the already complete fifteen-arrow lower bound.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A trivial action side gives an actual act-cone model: If one side of a finite biset action is trivial and its collage has type $\mathbb CP^2$, the corresponding ordinary act cone also has type $\mathbb CP^2$. A nontrivial trivially acting corner can consequently be removed in a minimal model.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Commuting permutation actions: If both actions on a nonempty finite biset are by permutations, every rational degree-two product of its collage vanishes.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A bouquet on one side of a chart: Use the three corner monoids of Theorem~\ref{C:affine-chart-family-zero}: the initial corner is the identity-adjoined left-zero two-band, the middle corner is trivial, and the final corner is the identity-adjoined right-zero two-band. Let $A,B$ be the natural graphs of the two adjacent acts, and let $K=K(T)$ be the cubical model of the long-edge biset. Suppose every component of $A$ is a bouquet of loops; isolated vertices are allowed. The graph $B$ and the composition may be arbitrary. If the whole category has rational second cohomology of dimension at most one, its degree-two square is zero. The same conclusion holds with $A,B$ interchanged.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: With the same three corner monoids, if either adjacent act has at most three states, the category cannot have the rational cohomology ring of $\CP^2$, regardless of the other two hom-set sizes.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Finite affine diagrams on a common rational grid: Let $D$ be a finite category and let $T:D^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Set}$ be a finite right act. Suppose each $T_i$ is the set of all points of $\delta\mathbb Z$ in a nonempty closed interval $I_i$ whose endpoints lie in $\delta\mathbb Z$, where $\delta>0$ is fixed and rational. Suppose every act map is the restriction of an affine map $I_j\to I_i$ of slope $0,1$, or $-1$. Degenerate intervals are allowed. Then every positive-degree rational cohomology product of the act cone is zero.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The categorical two-row act obstruction: Let $S$ be a finite strongly connected category. If every object has at most two rows in its minimal Rees ideal, then every product of rational degree-two classes on the cone of any nonempty finite right $S$-act is zero. There is no restriction on the maximal group of the minimal ideal or on the number of states. Dually, at most two minimal columns at each object exclude such products on every finite left-act cone.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The same degree-two product obstruction applies when the trivial sink of the preceding theorem is replaced by a finite monoid $N$ whose trivial right rational module is projective, and the cross sets form compatible $(N,S)$-actions. No finite-type hypothesis is required for this assertion.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $S$ be a finite strongly connected category on two objects with at most fourteen arrows. Adjoin a trivial sink with a nonempty finite right $S$-act. If the resulting category has at most twenty-one arrows, it cannot have type $\mathbb CP^2$. The dual assertion holds for an adjoined trivial source.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $S$ be a finite category with an object $a$ for which $1\leq|S(a,i)|\leq2$ at every object $i$. For every finite right $S$-act whose stalks are all nonempty, every rational degree-two product of its act cone is zero.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $S$ be a finite category, $a$ an object, $e\in\operatorname{End}_S(a)$ an idempotent, and $G$ a finite subgroup of the unit group of $e\operatorname{End}_S(a)e$. Suppose that the right $G$-orbit set $S(a,i)e/G$ has one or two elements at every object $i$. For every finite right $S$-act with all stalks nonempty, all rational degree-two products of its act cone vanish. The conclusion remains true after replacing the trivial sink by a monoid with projective trivial right rational module.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Affine representatives for balanced degree-two classes: Let $C$ be a finite strongly connected category with rectangular-band minimal ideal. Use the row and column sets $R_i,C_i$ and the augmentation modules $V,W$ of Lemma~\ref{C:category-band-Tor}. Suppose $\dim V=1$. Then every class in $H^2(BC;\mathbb Q)$ has an affine cocycle representative of the following form. There is a unique object $a$ with $|R_a|=2$, while every other $R_i$ is a singleton. Choose functions $a_i:R_i\to\mathbb Q$ and $b_i:C_i\to\mathbb Q$, both zero away from object $a$, and with chosen distinguished values zero. For each arrow $f:i\to j$ there are scalars $\chi_f,a_f,b_f$ such that \begin{align*} a_j\sigma_f&=\chi_f a_i+a_f,& b_i\tau_f&=\chi_f b_j+b_f. \end{align*} Here $\sigma_f:R_i\to R_j$ and $\tau_f:C_j\to C_i$ are the row and column actions, and $\chi_f=0$ unless $i=j=a$. For a composable pair written in multiplication order, \[ u(f,g)=b_fa_g \] represents the prescribed degree-two class.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The category rank-one cup obstruction: Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{C:category-band-Tor}, if $\dim V\leq1$ or $\dim W\leq1$, then every product of two rational degree-two classes is zero. Thus a nonzero such product requires \[ \sum_i r_i\geq |\operatorname{Ob}C|+2, \qquad \sum_i c_i\geq |\operatorname{Ob}C|+2. \] No finite-homotopy hypothesis is needed.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Rational Tor comparison with a finite minimal group: The Tor formula of Lemma~\ref{C:category-band-Tor} remains valid when the minimal group $G$ is any finite group, if $V,W$ are defined by the orbit augmentations \[ P=Re\otimes_{\mathbb QG}\mathbb Q\longrightarrow\mathbf1_\ell, \qquad Q=\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb QG}eR\longrightarrow\mathbf1_r. \] Their dimensions are still $\sum_i(r_i-1)$ and $\sum_i(c_i-1)$, and $A=R/\mathbb QK$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The strongly connected two-object exclusion through twenty: A finite category with two objects, nonempty hom-sets in both directions, and at most twenty arrows cannot have classifying space homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb{CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $C$ be a finite strongly connected category with a rectangular-band minimal ideal. If each object has at most two minimal rows, every product of rational degree-two classes on $BC$ is zero. The same statement holds if each object has at most two minimal columns. No finite-homotopy hypothesis is needed.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $C$ be a finite category with two objects $A,B$ and a rectangular-band minimal ideal. Suppose its row counts are $(3,1)$ and its column counts are $(3,1)$, with both triples at $A$. If $BC$ has finite CW homotopy type, every product of two rational degree-two classes on $BC$ is zero.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The strongly connected two-object exclusion through twenty-two: A finite category with two objects, nonempty hom-sets in both directions, and at most twenty-two arrows cannot have classifying space homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb{CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Constant minimal-ideal act compression: Let $M$ be a finite monoid with proper minimal ideal $K$, and let $I$ be the set of its minimal right ideals (the row set of its Rees matrix presentation). Let $S$ be a nonempty finite right $M$-set. Suppose that every $k\in K$ acts on $S$ as a constant map. There is an explicitly defined finite monoid $N$ with \[ |N|=|M|-|K|+|I|\,|S| \quad\hbox{and}\quad BN\simeq B\mathcal C(M,S). \] Here $\mathcal C(M,S)$ has objects $a,b$, endomorphism monoids $M,\{1_b\}$, hom-set $\Hom(a,b)=S$, and no arrows from $b$ to $a$. The conclusion allows nontrivial maximal groups in $K$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A numerical obstruction from the monoid minimum: Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{C:constant-minimal-act-compression}, if $B\mathcal C(M,S)\simeq\mathbb CP^2$, then \[ |M|-|K|+|I|\,|S|\geq23. \]
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The constant-action hypothesis is essential to the formula: The theorem does not infer constant action from the number of states. In particular a nontrivial maximal group in $K$ can act nontrivially on a small orbit. Such an action must be treated separately before applying this compression. If $K=M$ is a group and its identity acts constantly, $S$ is a singleton and the act cone is contractible; this degenerate case needs no replacement construction.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The constant-action quotient detects degree two: Let $M$ be any finite monoid with minimal ideal $K$, and let $S$ be a nonempty finite right $M$-set. Let $\bar S$ be the quotient of $S$ by the equivalence relation generated by \[ sk\sim s'k\qquad(s,s'\in S, k\in K). \] Then $\bar S$ is a right $M$-set on which every element of $K$ acts constantly. The induced functor of act cones gives a surjection \[ H^2(B\mathcal C(M,\bar S);\mathbb Q) \longrightarrow H^2(B\mathcal C(M,S);\mathbb Q). \] If $K$ is a rectangular band, the same surjection holds with integral coefficients. In particular, if $|S|\leq3$ and some element of $K$ does not act constantly on $S$, all degree-two rational products on $B\mathcal C(M,S)$ vanish. No restriction on the maximal group of $K$ is imposed.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A three-by-six band with five outside elements: A finite monoid with rectangular-band minimal ideal of shape $3\times6$ or $6\times3$, and exactly five elements outside that ideal, cannot have classifying space $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The exact three-state act-cone minimum: If a three-state act cone $\mathcal C(M,S)$ has classifying space $\mathbb CP^2$, then it has at least twenty-two arrows. This bound is attained by the two models of Theorem~\ref{C:CP2-upper22}.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: At most four states over a minimal band: Let $M$ have rectangular-band minimal ideal $K=I\times J$, and let $S$ be a nonempty finite right $M$-set with $|S|\leq4$. If $H_1(B\mathcal C(M,S);\mathbb Q)=0$, then either every degree-two rational cup product on this act cone is zero, or every element of $K$ acts constantly on $S$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Four-state cones through seventeen arrows: If $|S|=4$ and $|M|\leq12$, then $B\mathcal C(M,S)\not\simeq\mathbb CP^2$. Thus no four-state act cone with at most seventeen arrows models $\mathbb CP^2$. Also, if $|S|=3$, $|M|\leq15$, and the minimal ideal of $M$ is a band, the same exclusion holds.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A three-object triangle as a band extension: Let $M$ be a finite monoid, $S$ a nonempty finite left $M$-set, and $T$ a nonempty finite right $M$-set. Let $C$ have objects $0,1,2$, endomorphism monoids $\{1_0\},M,\{1_2\}$, and \[ \Hom_C(0,1)=S,\qquad \Hom_C(1,2)=T,\qquad \Hom_C(0,2)=\{w\}, \] with no other arrows between distinct objects. Every composite $t s$ equals $w$. Then $BC\simeq BN$, where \[ N=M\sqcup(S\times T),\qquad |N|=|M|+|S|\,|T|, \] and multiplication extends that of $M$ by \[ (s,t)(s',t')=(s,t'),\qquad m(s,t)=(ms,t),\qquad (s,t)m=(s,tm). \]
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A category in Theorem~\ref{C:triangle-band-compression} with $BC\simeq\mathbb CP^2$ satisfies $|M|+|S|\,|T|\geq23$. In particular the fifteen-arrow profile \[ (|\End(0)|,|\End(1)|,|\End(2)|, |\Hom(0,1)|,|\Hom(1,2)|,|\Hom(0,2)|) =(1,8,1,2,2,1) \] is impossible: its compressed monoid would have only twelve elements.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A stable retract propagates Tor: Let $R$ be a finite-dimensional algebra over a field, let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional left module, and choose projective syzygies $U=\Omega^2Q$ and $V=\Omega^{2+s}Q$, where $s\geq1$. Suppose there are homomorphisms \[ F_i:U\longrightarrow V,\quad G_i:V\longrightarrow U, \qquad A_j:U\longrightarrow P_j,\quad B_j:P_j\longrightarrow U, \] with every $P_j$ projective, such that \[ 1_U=\sum_i G_iF_i+\sum_j B_jA_j. \tag{\ref{C:stable-retract-Tor}.1} \] Then, for every right module $L$ and every $n\geq3$, \[ \operatorname{Tor}_n^R(L,Q)\ne0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \operatorname{Tor}_{n+s}^R(L,Q)\ne0. \] If the first sum is empty, $U$ is projective and all these degree-$n$ groups are zero.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A derived local Frobenius comparison: Let $R$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra and let $A$ be a quotient algebra which is local and Frobenius, with unique simple module $k$ and $\operatorname{pd}_R A\leq1$ on the left. Suppose a finite-dimensional left $R$-module $Q$ fits into \[ 0\longrightarrow k\longrightarrow P\longrightarrow Q \longrightarrow0, \] where $P$ is projective and the first module is obtained by restriction from the simple $A$-module. For every finite-dimensional right $R$-module $L$, eventual vanishing of $\operatorname{Tor}_n^R(L,Q)$ implies its vanishing for every $n\geq3$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: No projective-plane act cone over eight elements: For every finite monoid $M$ of order at most eight and every nonempty finite right $M$-set $S$, the category $\mathcal C(M,S)$ of Lemma~\ref{C:act-cone-Tor} does not have classifying space homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb CP^2$. There is no bound on the cardinality of $S$. The same exclusion holds for a triangular biset category with other endomorphism monoid $N$ whenever the trivial left $\mathbb QN^{\mathrm{op}}$-module is projective.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The all-core six-state obstruction: Suppose $|M|\leq9$, its minimal ideal is a rectangular band with two or three columns, $|S|\leq6$, and $S=SK$. Then the graph cofiber above cannot have type $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The complete two-core-orbit normal forms: If an $(R_4,M)$-collage with $|M|=8$, $|S|=6$ has type $\mathbb CP^2$, it occurs among the following normal forms over the complete $516$-table eight-element source cover: \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{minimal band}&|A|&|B|&\text{transient states}\\\hline 2\times2\text{ or }3\times2&2&2&2\\ 2\times3&2&2&2\\ 2\times3&2&3&1. \end{array} \] Here $A$ is the core vertex orbit, $B$ the core outside-state orbit, and every $P_i$ is the unique column-label map from $B$ to $A$. In the second row their two-part column partitions agree. In the last row the partition of $B$ is discrete. All three two-part partitions of the original three-column set are retained.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The finite three-retraction enumeration: The normal forms in Lemma~\ref{C:eight-R4-six-core-normalforms} have the following complete, independently verified enumeration: \[ \begin{array}{l|r} \text{source tables}&516\\ \text{column-partition/gamma profiles}&5856\\ \text{raw right actions on sorted profiles}&58968\\ \text{right-action state orbits}&45692\\ \text{unordered left triples over right representatives}&144487\\ \text{ordered left triples over right representatives}&503832\\ \text{retained literal categories}&126414. \end{array} \] Every retained category is excluded by its mod-two homology or its degree-two square. The separate independent source and literal-bar gates are recorded below.

statement: The right-zero-three-band corner through eight sources: No $(R_4,M)$-collage with $|M|\leq8$ and $|S|\leq6$ has type $\mathbb CP^2$.

statement: All order-four corners with eight source elements and six states: The eighteen-arrow two-object profile $(8,4,6)$ cannot realize $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: All image controls through order eight: The complete equal-loop and isolated-vertex action-image inventories through order eight contain $56+93=149$ literal monoids. Their rational graph-cofiber classifications are \[ \begin{array}{c|r} H_1\ne0&5\\ \dim H_2\geq2&4\\ H_1=0,\ H_2=\mathbb Q,\ \text{square zero}&77\\ H_1=H_2=0&63. \end{array} \] The last row consists precisely of nineteen order-seven images and forty-four order-eight images, all in the isolated-vertex family. The nineteen order-seven records are exactly the ones in the previous complete $660$-lift calculation.

statement: Rational six-state graph cups through source order eight: Let $|M|\leq8$, and let $M$ act on a finite oriented graph with $|V|+|E|\leq6$ by orientation-preserving unit-speed edge maps and edge collapses. Suppose its graph cofiber $X$ satisfies \[ H_1(X;\mathbb Q)=0,\qquad H^2(X;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q. \] Then its degree-two square vanishes. No finite-CW-type or bounded higher-homology hypothesis is needed.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Five four-element corners at the first new six-state profile: Let $|M|\leq8$, $|S|\leq6$, and suppose the four-element opposite corner has minimal ideal a two-element right-zero band. Its collage cannot have type $\mathbb CP^2$. In particular all five such corners are excluded in the eighteen-arrow profile $(8,4,6)$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $C$ be a connected finite category with $k$ objects and $n$ arrows. Suppose no object is a retract of another, $C$ has a proper strongly connected component on two objects, and \[ n\leq\min\{21,2k+8\}. \] Then $BC$ is not homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A category of type $\mathbb CP^2$ with eighteen arrows and at least four objects has either four objects, or five objects and acyclic support. In the five-object case its corner, parallel and support-cycle excesses satisfy $D+P+R=9$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A singleton and a three-state right-zero stalk: Let $S$ be a finite two-object category, let $R=\{1,p,q\}$ be the identity-adjoined right-zero two-band, and let compatible left $R$-sets and right $S$-actions form the cross sets of a collage with source block $S$ and sink corner $R$. Suppose the two stalk sizes are one and three. If all degree-two rational products vanish on every ordinary finite right $S$-act cone, then a one-dimensional second rational cohomology group of this collage has zero square.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Two-state actions of the five-element sphere band: Let $N$ be the identity-adjoined $2\times2$ rectangular band, and let $S$ be a finite strongly connected category with contractible classifying space. Suppose every cross stalk of an $(N,S)$-collage has two elements, and $H^2(BS;\mathbb Q)=0$. Then the collage cannot have the rational cohomology ring of $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Every finite category with three objects, at most eighteen arrows, and a nontrivial strongly connected component is excluded from type $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ be a finite monoid with $|M|\leq11$ and let $S$ be any nonempty finite right $M$-set. If its ordinary act cone has bounded rational homology, then every product of two rational degree-two classes is zero. Neither a first-homology condition nor a bound on the second-cohomology rank is required.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $C$ have outward star support with any positive number of leaves. Suppose its central monoid $M$ has at most eleven elements and the trivial right rational module at every leaf monoid is projective. If $BC$ has bounded rational homology, then every rational degree-two product on $BC$ is zero. The inward-star assertion is dual, with left modules at the leaves. There is no bound on the numbers of cross arrows.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A fixed incoming arrow: Let $C$ be a finite category whose objects consist of a full subcategory $D$ and one additional object $v$, with no arrows from $v$ to $D$. Write $M=\operatorname{End}_C(v)$. Suppose $H^2(BD;\mathbb Q)=0$ and there is an arrow $f:d\to v$, for some $d\in D$, such that $mf=f$ for every $m\in M$. Then \[ H^2(BC;\mathbb Q)\otimes H^2(BC;\mathbb Q) \longrightarrow H^4(BC;\mathbb Q) \] is the zero map. The opposite assertion holds for a source object and a fixed outgoing arrow.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The extreme eight-element corner at fifteen arrows: None of the following linear three-object cardinality profiles, nor any of their opposites, can have type $\mathbb{CP}^2$: \[ (m,n,p,x,y,z)=(1,1,8,2,1,2),\quad (1,1,8,2,2,1),\quad (2,1,8,1,1,2). \] Here $(m,n,p)$ are the endomorphism orders at $0,1,2$ and $(x,y,z)$ are the cardinalities of the hom-sets from $0$ to $1$, from $1$ to $2$, and from $0$ to $2$, respectively. No classification of the eight-element corner is required.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: At least three objects and fifteen arrows: A finite category with at least three objects and at most fifteen arrows cannot have classifying space homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb {CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The global lower bound of sixteen arrows: Every finite category whose classifying space is homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb {CP}^2$ has at least sixteen arrows, identities counted. Together with the explicit construction, the minimum-arrow interval is $16$--$22$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A three-object category with star support and at most fifteen arrows cannot have classifying space homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb {CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Deleting a retract-supported vertex: Let $C$ contain distinct objects $a,b$ such that $\End_C(b)=\{1_b,e\}$ with $e^2=e\ne1_b$. Suppose $e$ fixes every arrow incident to $b$ and another object: $ep=p$ for $p:x\to b$, $pe=p$ for $p:b\to x$, $x\ne b$. If there are $u:b\to a$, $v:a\to b$ with $vu=e$, then deleting $b$ preserves the homotopy type of the classifying space.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $S$ be the eleven-arrow two-object category formed by a rectangular minimal ideal with three total rows and three total columns, and one additional identity at each object. Suppose each object has at least one row and one column. Form $C$ by adjoining a sink $c$ with $\End(c)=\{1_c\}$ and three total arrows from $S$ to $c$, with arbitrary compatible actions. Then $BC$ does not have the homotopy type of $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A connected finite category on $k$ objects has at least $2k-1$ arrows. If equality holds, its classifying space is contractible. Consequently a fifteen-arrow category realizing $\mathbb{CP}^2$ has at most seven objects.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $|M|\leq9$, let $S$ be a nonempty finite right $M$-set, and suppose the act cone $X=B\mathcal C(M,S)$ has bounded rational homology and $\dim H^2(X;\mathbb Q)\leq1$. Every degree-two square is zero. No assumption on $H^1(X;\mathbb Q)$ is needed.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A three-object category with at most fifteen arrows and a nontrivial strongly connected component does not realize $\mathbb{CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Star reductions at fifteen arrows: For an outward three-object star of total size fifteen, let $(m,a,b,x,y)$ denote the central and leaf endomorphism orders and the two leg sizes. The generic star exclusions in Lemma~\ref{C:generic-star-deletions} still hold, with each bound eight there replaced by nine. There is also an exclusion when $m\leq4$ and $x,y\leq2$. The same assertions hold for inward stars. If every vertex has zero rational $H^2$, the star is excluded as before.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The rational all-act obstruction at order ten: Let $|M|=10$ and let $S$ be any nonempty finite right $M$-set. If the act cone has bounded rational homology, then all of its rational degree-two products vanish. In particular it cannot have the rational cohomology ring of $\mathbb{CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Three states opposite a two-element right-zero band: Let $N=\{1,p,q\}$, with $p^2=p$, $q^2=q$, $pq=q$, and $qp=p$. Let $S$ be a three-element $(N,M)$-biset. If its collage has type $\mathbb{CP}^2$, then an ordinary right $M$-act cone on at most three states has that type. Consequently no such collage with $|M|\leq17$ has type $\mathbb{CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The complete fifteen-arrow triangular calculation: No triangular finite category with two objects and at most fifteen arrows has classifying space homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb{CP}^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

For the new certificates, a separate normalized-bar implementation rebuilds every literal category, checks all typed associativity equations, verifies its second Betti number and the nonboundary generator, and checks every claimed primitive on every degree-four simplex. The alternative certificates are checked by independent third-homology ranks. All seventeen profiles pass this independent verification: $2510793$ retained certificates, $1859788417$ typed associativity equations, $1167434995$ cocycle equations, and $7023259440$ primitive equations. statement: A finite category with at most two objects and classifying space homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb{CP}^2$ has at least sixteen arrows.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Projective trivial modules and the minimal column: Let $N$ be a finite monoid with minimal Rees ideal $I\times G\times J$. The trivial right $\mathbb QN$-module is projective if and only if $|J|=1$. In this case a minimal idempotent $e$ satisfies $eN=eNe=G$, and \[ q_N:N\longrightarrow G,\qquad n\longmapsto en \] is a unital monoid homomorphism, with $e$ the identity of $G$. Over a field of characteristic $p$, the same trivial right module is projective if and only if $|J|=1$ and $p\nmid|G|$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The equivariant action-groupoid comparison: Let $N$ satisfy the preceding lemma, and let $S$ be a left $N$-set with a commuting right action by a monoid $M$. Let $S\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}N$ denote its left action category. There is an actual right-$M$-equivariant functor \[ p:S\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}N \longrightarrow eS\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}G, \qquad s\longmapsto es,\quad n\longmapsto en, \] which induces a weak equivalence of classifying spaces. Moreover $N\backslash S$ is the finite right $M$-set $T=G\backslash eS$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Finite-target and good-prime corner removal: Let $C$ be the triangular two-object category with endomorphism monoids $M,N$, cross-biset $S$ with left $N$-action and right $M$-action, and no reverse cross arrows. Assume the trivial right $\mathbb QN$-module is projective. Put $T=N\backslash S$ and let \[ Q:C\longrightarrow C(M,T) \] be the actual quotient functor, equal to the identity on $M$, sending $N$ to the identity at the other object and $S$ to $T$. Then: \begin{enumerate} \item $BQ$ induces an isomorphism of cohomology rings over $\mathbb Q$, and over $\mathbb F_p$ whenever $p\nmid|G|$. \item For every connected finite CW complex $X$, precomposition is a weak equivalence of derived unbased mapping spaces \[ \operatorname{Map}(BC(M,T),X) \longrightarrow \operatorname{Map}(BC,X). \] \item If $BC$ has finite CW homotopy type, there is a homotopy left inverse $h:BC(M,T)\to BC$ to $BQ$. \end{enumerate} The size of the act category is $|M|+|T|+1\leq|M|+|S|+1$. No assertion that it has finite CW type or the same integral homology as $BC$ is included.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The precise projective-plane consequences: In the setting of the preceding theorem, suppose $BC\simeq\mathbb CP^2$. Write $Y=BC(M,T)$ and let $u$ be an integral generator of $H^2(BC;\mathbb Z)$. Then $Y$ is simply connected and has the rational and good-prime cohomology rings of $\mathbb CP^2$. There is a class $v\in H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$ with \[ (BQ)^*v=u,\qquad (BQ)^*(v^2)=u^2. \] The group $H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)$ is infinite cyclic, $v$ is a generator, and $v^2$ is primitive in the free quotient of $H^4(Y;\mathbb Z)$. For every finite group $H$ and every map $a:BH\to Y$, the composite $h a:BH\to BC$ is null-homotopic, and $a^*v=0$ integrally.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A trivial minimal group gives an actual equivalence: In Theorem~\ref{C:finite-target-opposite-corner}, suppose the minimal local group of $N$ is trivial. Then the actual quotient $BC\to BC(M,N\backslash S)$ is a homotopy equivalence. Consequently, if $BC\simeq\mathbb CP^2$, then \[ |C|\ \geq\ 21+|N|+|S|-|N\backslash S|. \] In particular a nontrivial such opposite corner cannot occur in a projective-plane category with at most $22$ arrows.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Finite-target detection after an orbit quotient: Let $X=B\mathcal C(M,S)$ satisfy Lemma~\ref{C:two-column-projective-orbit-kernel}, and suppose $X$ is simply connected. Suppose a map $h:X\to F$ to a simply connected finite CW complex induces an isomorphism on integral second cohomology. Write $Y=B\mathcal C(M,\bar S)$ and let $o$ be the number of core orbits. Then there is a map \[ Y\longrightarrow F\vee\bigvee_{o-1}S^2 \] inducing an isomorphism on integral second cohomology. In particular every integral second-cohomology class on $Y$ restricts to zero along every map $BH\to Y$ from a finite group.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Scope of the smaller act cone: Corollary~\ref{C:finite-target-corner-CP2} gives a finite-source nullity condition for every local-group restriction of the distinguished class $v$. It does not identify the integral homotopy type of $Y$. In particular a lower bound that assumes $Y$ itself has finite CW type cannot be applied merely from this comparison. Universal rational cup primitives and certified field cup obstructions do apply through (1); any imported finite-type hull argument must separately check that its use of finiteness is exactly the local-group nullity supplied by the corollary.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The precise finite-target uses in the small band hulls: Let $P$ be a finite monoid with rectangular-band minimal ideal. Assume that every integral class in $H^2(BP;\mathbb Z)$ restricts to zero along every map from the classifying space of a finite group. Then the following consequences of the earlier hull calculations hold. \begin{enumerate} \item For a $3\times3$ band, all rational degree-two products vanish. \item For a $3\times4$ band with rational second-cohomology rank two, all rational degree-two products vanish. \item For a $3\times4$ band with rational second-cohomology rank one, the square of an integral generator cannot be nonzero and primitive modulo torsion in fourth cohomology. \end{enumerate} The same statements hold after opposition. There is no finite-CW-type assumption on $BP$ in this lemma.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Nullity survives the projective orbit quotient: Let $X=B\mathcal C(M,S)$ be simply connected, with minimal band $I\times\{0,1\}$ and no band-fixed state. Suppose every integral second-cohomology class of $X$ restricts to zero on every finite $BG$. The constant-action quotient and its compression $Y\simeq BP$ have the same nullity property in degree two.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The rational five-outside row argument at six states: Let $M$ have minimal band $4\times2$ and exactly five outside elements. An act cone on five or six states cannot have the rational homology and cohomology ring of $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A finite-target obstruction through twenty act arrows: Let $X=B\mathcal C(M,S)$ for a nonempty finite right act, with $|M|+|S|+1\leq20$. The following conditions cannot hold simultaneously: \begin{enumerate} \item $X$ is simply connected and its rational homology is that of $\mathbb CP^2$; \item an integral generator $v\in H^2(X;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ has square nonzero and primitive modulo torsion in $H^4(X;\mathbb Z)$; \item for every finite group $G$ and every map $BG\to X$, the restriction of $v$ is zero; \item over $\mathbb F_{65521}$, the Betti numbers in degrees two, three and four are $(1,0,1)$. \end{enumerate} In particular no finite-CW-type assumption on $X$ is required.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Nontrivial projective opposite corners through twenty-one arrows: Let $C$ be a triangular two-object category with endomorphism monoids $M,N$, cross-biset ${}_NS_M$, and projective trivial right $\mathbb QN$-module. If $|N|\geq2$ and $|C|\leq21$, then $BC\not\simeq\mathbb CP^2$. The same conclusion holds with $|C|\leq22$ and $|N|\geq3$. Both statements also hold after opposition.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The remaining two-object scope: The argument treats the precise finite-target hypotheses above, rather than declaring every rational projective-plane act cone to have finite CW type. At twenty-one arrows, an unexcluded triangular category must fail both projective-corner tests: its source corner must have at least two minimal rows and its target corner at least two minimal columns. This follows by applying the corollary also to the opposite category. It does not dispose of these nonprojective opposite corners. Strongly connected two-object categories are resolved separately by Theorem~\ref{C:twentytwo-strongly-connected}; the present theorem itself concerns only triangular categories. The original unrestricted category minimum is not asserted here.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $C$ have five objects, trivial endomorphism monoids, and acyclic support. If $C$ has at most twenty-one arrows, then $BC\not\simeq\mathbb {CP}^2$.

Up to ordinary monoid isomorphism it belongs to the following three necessary source lists: \[ \begin{array}{c|r|r} \text{row levels}&\substack{\text{nonconstant image}\\\text{orbits}}& \text{source monoids}\\\hline 4+1&14&33\\ 3+2&183&60223\\ (-1,-1,0,0,1)&2&12. \end{array} \]

Their exact certificate partition is \[ \begin{array}{c|r|r|r|r|r} \text{levels}&\operatorname{pd}V\leq1&\substack{\text{stable}\\\text{Tor}}& \substack{\text{local simple}\\\text{tail}}&\substack{\text{even degree-two}\\\text{Tor}}& \substack{\text{remaining}\\\operatorname{pd}V\leq2}\\\hline 4+1&24&9&0&0&0\\ 3+2&35683&22951&22&20&1547\\ (-1,-1,0,0,1)&12&0&0&0&0. \end{array} \] For a stable or local simple tail, eventual vanishing of the Tor groups implies \[ \operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)=0 \] for every finite-dimensional right $A$-module $W$. In the next column this degree-two group has even dimension for every $W$.

statement: Five rows and four states: Let $M$ have minimal band $5\times2$ and six outside elements. No four-state right act has cone of type $\mathbb CP^2$.

More precisely, $H$ lies in one of five explicit actor monoids with zero fourth rational homology.

statement: A five-state three-by-two obstruction: Let $M$ be a finite monoid with rectangular-band minimal ideal of shape $3\times2$, and let $S$ be a right $M$-set with five elements. Then \[ B\mathcal C(M,S)\not\simeq\mathbb CP^2. \] There is no bound on the number of elements of $M$ in this statement.

statement: Scope and computational controls: The preceding theorem assumes a minimal band, not a nontrivial minimal maximal group. It uses complete finite actor calculations only in the already classified three-by-three and three-by-five hulls and in the five new zero-homology witnesses above; it does not enumerate monoids of unbounded order. As a separate control, all $1082$ two-core-orbit five-state normal forms over the $272$ nonsplit-row order-ten residual targets were checked in \path{code/a_five_state_two_orbits.py}. Of these, $1050$ fail exact rational homology through degree three and the other $32$ have explicit mod-two square primitives. statement: The rational five-state graph obstruction for small sources: Let $M$ have order at most nine and act on a graph with vertex set $U$ and oriented edge set $E$, where $|U|+|E|\leq5$. Every actor sends each oriented edge at unit speed to another oriented edge or collapses it to a vertex. If the cofiber of its action-bar projection to $BM$ has one-dimensional second rational cohomology, the square of that class is zero.

statement: An explicit normalized action-groupoid presentation: Let $N=\{1,p,q,x\}$ have minimal right-zero ideal $\{p,q\}$, and let $S$ be a left $N$-set. Write $P,Q,E$ for the actions of $p,q,x$, and let $U$ be the common image of $P,Q$. In the fundamental groupoid of $N\ltimes S$, identify each object $s$ with $Ps$ using the arrow labeled $p$. The resulting groupoid on $U$ has one oriented generator $g_s:Ps\to Qs$ for each $s\notin U$, with $g_u=1$ for $u\in U$, and precisely these relations: \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{right action of $x$ on $\{p,q\}$}&\text{relations}\\\hline \mathrm{id}&g_{Es}=g_s\\ \mathrm{constant}_p&g_{Es}=1\\ \mathrm{swap}&g_{Es}=g_s^{-1}. \end{array} \] The constant case may be arranged to be $p$ by relabeling. The presentation and its functor from the actual action category are natural for every commuting right action.

statement: Five states for the five two-band order-four corners: Suppose $|N|=4$, its minimal ideal is a right-zero band of size two, $|M|\leq9$, and $|S|\leq5$ in an $(N,M)$-biset. If the collage has one-dimensional second rational cohomology, its generator has square zero. In particular none of these collages has type $\mathbb CP^2$.

statement: Nonconstant six-state four-row acts: Let $M$ have minimal band $4\times2$ and at most six outside elements. statement: Let $C$ be a four-object outward or inward star category with at most fifteen arrows. Write $M$ for its central endomorphism monoid, $A_1,A_2,A_3$ for the leaf monoids, and $s_1,s_2,s_3$ for the nonempty leg cardinalities. Each of the following conditions excludes $BC\simeq\mathbb {CP}^2$: \begin{enumerate} \item Every $|A_i|\leq4$, and some $s_i=1$. \item $|M|\leq9$ and every $|A_i|\leq2$. \item At least two of $s_1,s_2,s_3$ equal one. \end{enumerate}

statement: Let $C$ be a finite category on objects $0,1,2$, with no backward arrows and with trivial endomorphism monoids at $0$ and $2$. Suppose the three forward hom-sets are nonempty. Put \[ N=\operatorname{End}_C(1),\quad R=\mathbb QN,\quad V=\mathbb QC(0,1),\quad W=\mathbb QC(1,2),\quad U=\mathbb QC(0,2). \] Here $V$ is a left $R$-module, $W$ is a right $R$-module, and all three permutation spaces have their usual augmentation to $\mathbb Q$. Write $\bar V,\bar W,\bar U$ for the respective augmentation kernels. Then, naturally, \begin{equation} H_n(BC;\mathbb Q)\cong \operatorname{Tor}^{R}_{n-2}(\bar W,\bar V) \qquad(n\geq3). \end{equation} There is also an exact sequence \[ 0\longrightarrow H_2(BC;\mathbb Q) \longrightarrow\bar W\otimes_R\bar V \xrightarrow{\bar\mu}\bar U \longrightarrow H_1(BC;\mathbb Q) \longrightarrow0, \] where $\bar\mu$ is induced by the actual composition $C(1,2)\times C(0,1)\to C(0,2)$.

statement: Let $C$ have three linearly ordered objects and nonempty forward hom-sets. Suppose its two endpoint monoid algebras are semisimple over $\mathbb Q$. If its middle monoid has at most four elements, or has a two-sided zero and at most five elements, bounded rational homology of $BC$ implies \[ H_4(BC;\mathbb Q)=0. \] In particular these categories cannot have type $\mathbb CP^2$, at any cross-hom cardinalities.

statement: Collapsing the long hom-set: Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{C:linear-augmentation-Tor}, let $D$ retain every object and arrow of $C$ except that all arrows $0\to2$ are identified to a single arrow. Composition into that hom-set is the unique possible map. This defines a category and an actual functor $C\to D$. If $BC$ is simply connected and $u=|C(0,2)|$, then \[ BD\simeq BC\vee\bigvee^{u-1}S^2. \] In particular, if $BC\simeq\mathbb CP^2$, the triangle-compression monoid of order $|N|+|C(0,1)|\,|C(1,2)|$ realizes $\mathbb CP^2\vee\bigvee^{u-1}S^2$.

statement: The graph retraction for constant composition: Let $C$ have objects $0,1,2$, trivial endomorphism monoids at $0$ and $2$, middle endomorphism monoid $N$, and nonempty forward hom sets $S=C(0,1)$, $T=C(1,2)$ and $U=C(0,2)$. Suppose there are no other arrows between distinct objects. If all composites $ts$, with $s\in S$ and $t\in T$, equal a single $u_0\in U$, the two-object category with $|U|$ parallel arrows is an actual categorical retract of $C$. In particular $\bigvee^{|U|-1}S^1$ is a homotopy retract of $BC$.

statement: Constant profiles force constant composition: In the setting of Lemma~\ref{C:linear-constant-composition-retract}, suppose there is $t_0\in T$ such that for every $s\in S$ some $n_s\in N$ acts constantly on $S$ with value $s$ and constantly on $T$ with value $t_0$. Then all composites $ts$ have the same value. The analogous assertion holds after interchanging $S,T$ and taking the opposite category.

statement: The eight closed-actor controls: Consider the eight specified faithful rank-two order-twenty action models in \path{code/outputs/d_rank_two_small_inflation_controls.json}. Generate a middle actor submonoid from the identity and all three nonband actors. With adjacent hom-set sizes four and four and a two-element long hom set, none of these controls produces a category of type $\mathbb CP^2$ through twenty-one arrows.

statement: Two long arrows and four arrows on each adjacent side: Let $C$ have three linearly ordered objects $0,1,2$, trivial endomorphism monoids at $0$ and $2$, and no backward arrows. Suppose \[ |C(0,1)|=|C(1,2)|=4,\qquad |C(0,2)|=2. \] If $C$ has at most twenty-one arrows, then $BC$ is not homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb CP^2$.

statement: The closed middle submonoid is essential to the size bound. Arbitrary monoids with the same small faithful image can have additional elements, and products of their outside elements may enter the minimal band. Here the triangle-compression construction retains the original closed middle monoid, so its entire transformation image, including constant profiles, costs at most nine elements. The theorem makes no claim for nontrivial endpoint monoids or for larger adjacent hom-sets.

statement: Second homology under the actual middle-action quotient: Let $C$ be a finite category on linearly ordered objects $0,1,2$, with trivial endpoint endomorphism monoids, nonempty forward hom-sets $I,J,U$, and no backward arrows. Replace the middle monoid $N$ by its joint action image $D$ on $I,J$, retaining the three hom-sets and their actual composition map. This gives a finite category $C_D$ and an actual quotient functor \[ F:C\longrightarrow C_D. \] For every field $k$, the induced maps on $H_1(-;k)$ and $H_2(-;k)$ are isomorphisms. Consequently every degree-two cohomology class on $BC$ is the pullback of one on $BC_D$, with its cup products preserved.

If the joint action image of its middle monoid on the adjacent hom-sets has at most ten elements, then $BC\not\simeq\mathbb CP^2$. If the joint action image of the middle monoid on the two adjacent hom-sets has at most ten elements, then $BC\not\simeq\CP^2$. statement: An affine pencil cannot give a lone positive even Tor group: Let $A$ be the rational algebra with basis $1,x,y,z,c$, with \[ x^2=z,\qquad xz=zx=y^2=c,\qquad xy=\epsilon c,\qquad yx=(1-\epsilon)c, \qquad \epsilon\in\{0,1\}, \] and all other products between $x,y,z,c$ zero. For $a\in\mathbb Q$, let $V_a$ be the two-dimensional module on which $y$ acts as a nonzero square-zero Jordan block, $x$ acts as $a$ times that block, and $z,c$ act as zero. There is no finite-dimensional right $A$-module $W$ with \[ \operatorname{Tor}_1^A(W,V_a)=0,\qquad \dim\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V_a)=1,\qquad \operatorname{Tor}_n^A(W,V_a)=0\quad(n\geq3). \]

statement: Every local five-element contracted basis on three rows: Let $A$ be a local contracted rational algebra of a finite monoid, with $\dim A=5$. Suppose $V$ is a two-dimensional $A$-module with a fixed augmentation basis of a three-point set, in which every distinguished nonzero monoid basis element acts by the augmentation matrix of a transformation of that set. The transformations themselves need not descend through the contracted zero; only their augmentation operators are required to give the stated $A$-module. There is no finite-dimensional right module $W$ with \[ \operatorname{Tor}_1^A(W,V)=0,\qquad \dim\operatorname{Tor}_2^A(W,V)=1,\qquad \operatorname{Tor}_n^A(W,V)=0\quad(n\geq3). \]
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Local quotients with five outside elements: Let $M$ have rectangular-band minimal ideal of shape $3\times2$, with exactly five outside elements, and suppose $\mathbb QM/\mathbb QK$ is local. For every nonempty finite right $M$-set $S$, $B\mathcal C(M,S)$ cannot have the rational homology and cohomology ring of $\mathbb CP^2$. In particular it cannot be homotopy equivalent to $\mathbb CP^2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The one-edge-circle chart obstruction: Use the corner monoids and three-object support of Theorem~\ref{C:affine-chart-family-zero}. statement: Finite-target removal of an extreme corner: Let $C$ be a finite category with an object $b$ having no arrows to any other object.
