statement: Let $R=\Z Q_8$ and $N=\sum_{g\in Q_8}g$. The matrix \[ e_8=\begin{pmatrix}1-8N&21N\\-3N&8N\end{pmatrix} \] is idempotent, and its image has nonzero class in $\widetilde K_0(R)$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $R=\Z C_{23}=\Z[g]/(g^{23}-1)$, set $N=\sum_{a=0}^{22}g^a$, and put \[ \omega=1+g+g^2+g^3+g^4+g^6+g^8+g^9+g^{12}+g^{13}+g^{16}+g^{18}. \] Then \[ e_{23}=\begin{pmatrix} 4+8N&\omega-1+N\\ 2\omega-46N&-3-8N \end{pmatrix} \] is idempotent and $[\im e_{23}]\ne0$ in $\widetilde K_0(R)$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The program \texttt{d\_explicit\_projectives.py} gives both complete group tables, verifies all $512$ and $12\,167$ associativity triples, checks all integral coefficients of both projector identities, and computes the exact ranks $8$ and $23$ of their integral regular matrices. It also checks both complementary projectors. Nontriviality of a projective class is established by the proofs above, not inferred from a matrix rank calculation. These are algebraic inputs to the finite category construction; by themselves they are not counterexamples to Question D1.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: An explicit negative answer to D1: There is a connected finite category $\mathcal W_8$ with \[ \begin{split} |\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal W_8| &=489\,754\,140\,643\,145\,442,\\ |\operatorname{Mor}\mathcal W_8| &=337\,126\,384\,361\,511\,151\,079\,802. \end{split} \] Its classifying space is finitely dominated and has a CW model of dimension at most eight. Its fundamental group is $Q_8$, and \[ w(B\mathcal W_8)=[\operatorname{im}e_8]\ne0 \quad\text{in }\widetilde K_0(\mathbb ZQ_8). \] Consequently $B\mathcal W_8$ is not homotopy equivalent to a finite CW complex. The complete indexed table is implemented in \path{code/d_final_wall_category.py}. The function \texttt{build\_final\_category()} returns it as \texttt{Final}; its four operations are \texttt{source}, \texttt{target}, \texttt{identity}, and \texttt{compose}.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Representing a corner map by a finite biset: Let $P,M$ be finite monoids and let $\phi:P\to eMe$ be a unital homomorphism, where $e\in M$ is idempotent. Regard $Me$ as an $(M,P)$-biset using $\phi$ on the right. Its category of elements has classifying space homotopy equivalent to $BP$; under this equivalence its two projections induce the identity of $BP$ and the corner map $BP\to BM$ defined by $\phi$. Consequently, for any finite family $\phi_i:P\to e_iMe_i$, the two-object category with endomorphism monoids $P,M$, no arrows in the reverse direction, and cross-biset $\coprod_i Me_i$ realizes \[ \operatorname{hocolim}\left( BP\ \longleftarrow\ \coprod_i BP\ \longrightarrow\ BM\right), \] with left maps the identity and right maps the prescribed corner maps.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A two-object degree-two mapping torus: The mapping torus of a degree-two self-map of $S^2$ is the classifying space of a finite category with exactly two objects and aperiodic endomorphism monoids. Its fundamental group is $\mathbb Z$, and \[ H_2(\widetilde X;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z[1/2]. \] In particular, finite two-object categories are not restricted to wedges of circles and simply connected summands, nor to finite-order monodromy.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A wedge construction preserving full corners: Let $P,Q$ be finite aperiodic monoids whose classifying spaces have finite homotopy type. There is a finite aperiodic monoid $R$ and full-corner embeddings of $P,Q$ into $R$ such that \[ BR\simeq BP\vee BQ \] under the two corner maps. Each left and right ideal joining a corner to $1_R$ is a finite projective act over the corresponding corner monoid. Here a finite projective act means a retract of a finite free act, or equivalently a finite disjoint union of idempotent-generated principal ideals.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Relative cell trading: For a map $f:T\to X$ between finite connected simply connected CW complexes, there is a finite relative CW complex $Z$ built from $T$ using only cells of dimension at least two, and a homotopy equivalence $Z\simeq X$ whose restriction to $T$ represents $f$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Simultaneous full-corner realization: Let $T_1,\ldots,T_k,X$ be finite connected simply connected CW complexes, and let $f_i:T_i\to X$ be a finite family of maps. Fix finite aperiodic monoids $P_i$ realizing the $T_i$. There is a finite aperiodic monoid $M$ with full corners $e_iMe_i\cong P_i$ such that $BM\simeq X$ and the corner maps represent the $f_i$. The side acts $Me_i$ and $e_iM$ are finite projective $P_i$-acts.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A finite biset for a correspondence: Suppose $P$ embeds as full corners $e_A M_A e_A$ and $e_B M_B e_B$, with finite projective side acts. The finite $(M_B,M_A)$-biset \[ S=M_Be_B\otimes_P e_A M_A \] realizes the correspondence $BM_A\leftarrow BP\to BM_B$: its two-object collage has the homotopy type of this homotopy pushout, compatibly with the two vertex maps. A disjoint union of such bisets realizes the corresponding disjoint union of edge spaces.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Two objects realize finite graphs of simply connected spaces: Every finite connected graph of finite connected simply connected CW spaces, with arbitrary continuous edge attaching maps, has the homotopy type of the classifying space of a finite category with exactly two objects and aperiodic endomorphism monoids.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A graph as the one-skeleton: If $X$ is a finite connected CW complex with fundamental group $F_r$, then $X$ has a finite CW model whose two-skeleton is $R_r\vee\bigvee_{j=1}^a S^2$, where $R_r$ is a rose with $r$ petals.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Enlarging pieces over a tree: Let $Z$ be a finite graph of finite connected simply connected CW spaces over the rose $R_r$, and let $n\geq3$. For any map $\alpha:S^{n-1}\to Z$, the space $Z\cup_\alpha D^n$ again has a model of this form over the same rose.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Finite complexes with free fundamental group: A finite connected CW complex $X$ is homotopy equivalent to the classifying space of a finite category with exactly two objects if and only if its fundamental group is free. In the sufficient direction the endomorphism monoids can both be chosen aperiodic.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The full two-object classification: The connected finite-dimensional CW homotopy types realized by finite categories with exactly two objects are precisely the finite connected CW homotopy types with free fundamental group.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The tree enlargement proof uses no homology-preserving plus construction on the individual vertex or edge pieces. Their homology is allowed to change; the product with a contractible membership subtree controls the homotopy type of the total space.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The disconnected finite-dimensional types realized by categories with exactly two objects are precisely disjoint unions of two nonempty finite connected simply connected CW homotopy types.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M=\{1,a,b,c,d,y\}$, where $a=x_{00}$, $b=x_{01}$, $c=x_{10}$ and $d=x_{11}$. The identity is $1$, and \[ x_{ij}x_{k\ell}=x_{i\ell},\qquad yx_{ij}=x_{0j},\qquad x_{ij}y=x_{i0},\qquad y^2=a. \] Then \[ BM\simeq\bigvee_{n=2}^{\infty}S^n. \] Every integral Hurewicz homomorphism $\pi_n(BM)\to H_n(BM;\Z)$, $n\ge2$, is a split epimorphism. The integral cohomology ring is $\Z\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ge2}\Z u_n$, with $|u_n|=n$ and $u_pu_q=0$ for all $p,q\ge2$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: There is a finite monoid, of order six including its identity, for which $[BM,S^2]$ has cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. In particular the assertion that $[BC,S^2]$ is countable for every finite category is false.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ be a finite regular monoid with $j$ Green $\mathcal J$-classes. Then $H_n(BM;\Q)=0$ for $n>2(j-1)$. Consequently none of $K(\Z,2)$, $\Omega S^3$, $\Sigma\CP^\infty$ or $\bigvee_{n\ge2}S^n$ is the classifying space of a finite regular monoid.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ be a discrete monoid. For a normalized integral monoid two-cocycle $u:M\times M\to\Z$, let $E_u=M\times\Z$ with \[ (a,r)(b,s)=(ab,r+s+u(a,b)). \] There is a homotopy-fiber sequence \[ B\Z\longrightarrow BE_u\longrightarrow BM \] classified by $[u]\in H^2(BM;\Z)$, up to the choice of sign for the fiber generator. Consequently $BM\simeq K(\Z,2)$ if and only if some such $E_u$ has contractible classifying space. The extra hypothesis $U(M)=1$ in R9(H2) is necessary but redundant in this reformulation. For finite $M$, neither condition occurs, by Corollary~\ref{A:rational-nilpotence}.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $X$ be a connected CW complex with $H^1(X;\Z)=0$. If $S^n$ is a homotopy retract of $X$ for infinitely many distinct $n$ with $\pi_n(S^3)\ne0$, then both $[X,S^3]$ and $[X,S^2]$ are uncountable. The proof of \emph{OWN\_RESULTS}, Proposition 4.1, is correct.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a nonempty finite category with $v$ objects and $a$ arrows. There is an explicitly defined monoid $M_{\mathcal C}$ of order $1+a+(v+1)^2$ with rectangular-band minimal ideal and a natural stable equivalence \[ \widetilde{\Sigma^\infty BM_{\mathcal C}} \simeq \Sigma^2\Sigma^\infty(B\mathcal C)_+ . \] Every nontrivial maximal subgroup of $M_{\mathcal C}$ is a maximal subgroup of an endomorphism monoid of $\mathcal C$, and conversely. In particular, $M_{\mathcal C}$ is aperiodic if and only if all endomorphism monoids of $\mathcal C$ are aperiodic.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Fix a prime $p$. The assertion that the mod-$p$ cohomology of every finite monoid whose maximal subgroups have order prime to $p$ is locally finite over the Steenrod algebra is equivalent to the same assertion for all finite categories whose local subgroups have order prime to $p$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a finite category whose pointed consolidation $Q$ has a nilpotent ideal $N$ with regular quotient $Q/N$. At every prime avoiding the orders of the maximal subgroups of $Q/N$, the mod-$p$ cohomology of $B\mathcal C$ is locally finite over the Steenrod algebra. In particular $B\mathcal C$ cannot have the homotopy type of $\Sigma\mathbb{CP}^{\infty}$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Fix $p$. A pointed CW space with commuting cellular actions of finitely many finite monoids is \emph{controlled} if every joint actor image is a CW subcomplex and has finite total $\mathbb F_p$ homology. The identity actors are included, so the space itself has finite total homology. We use the usual mapping-cylinder and simplicial-replacement CW models; the explicit constructions below preserve this condition. Only finite total homology, not a finite number of cells, is required.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Locally finite unstable modules over the mod-$p$ Steenrod algebra are closed under submodules, quotients, and extensions. Consequently a finite sequence of pointed homotopy pushouts and cofibers of spaces with locally finite cohomology again has locally finite cohomology.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $R$ act on a controlled pointed space $X$ on the left, commuting with an external finite-monoid action. For a two-sided ideal $P\subseteq R$, let $\mathcal P(P)$ be the finite poset of principal right ideals $aR$ with $a\in P$, ordered by inclusion, and put \[ \mathcal F_P X=\mathop{\operatorname{hocolim}}_{aR\in\mathcal P(P)} aX. \] The zero image is the one-point space; the homotopy colimit is pointed. Equal principal right ideals give literally equal images. Then the following hold. \begin{enumerate} \item $\mathcal F_R X\to X$ is an $R$-equivariant underlying homotopy equivalence, also equivariant for the external action. \item Ideal inclusions induce CW-subcomplex inclusions between the chosen models. Left multiplication sends the diagram at $aR$ to that at $baR$, strictly functorially. \item Every joint actor image in $\mathcal F_P X$ has finite total mod-$p$ homology. Its intersection with $\mathcal F_T X$, for a smaller ideal $T\subseteq P$, also has finite total homology. Consequently all joint images in $\mathcal F_P X/\mathcal F_T X$ have finite total homology. \item If $P^h=0$, the spaces $F^sX=\mathcal F_{P^s}X$ ($P^0=R$) form a finite filtration, with strict multiplication maps $P^r\wedge F^sX\to F^{r+s}X$ for all $r,s\geq0$. \end{enumerate} There is a right-action version using principal left ideals.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $J$ be a minimal nonzero regular $\mathcal J$-class ideal of a finite pointed monoid $R$, and let $A=R/J$. A controlled left $R$-space $Y$, with a commuting external action, has a controlled actual left $A$-space $Y'$ and an equivariant underlying equivalence \[ Y'\simeq A\mathbin{\wedge_R^{\mathbb L}}Y. \] The same holds on the right. This comparison preserves the external actions and can therefore be used inside longer balanced bars.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $R_1,\ldots,R_k$ be finite pointed monoids, and let $X_0,\ldots,X_k$ be controlled pointed spaces with the commuting left and right actions needed to form \[ Z=X_0\mathbin{\wedge_{R_1}^{\mathbb L}}X_1 \mathbin{\wedge_{R_2}^{\mathbb L}}\cdots \mathbin{\wedge_{R_k}^{\mathbb L}}X_k. \] If $p$ divides none of the maximal-subgroup orders of these monoids, then $\widetilde H^*(Z;\mathbb F_p)$ is locally finite over the Steenrod algebra.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ be a finite monoid. At every prime not dividing the order of any maximal subgroup of $M$, the mod-$p$ cohomology of $BM$ is locally finite over the Steenrod algebra. The same statement holds for finite categories and their local subgroups.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The space $\Sigma\mathbb{CP}^{\infty}$ is not the classifying-space homotopy type of a finite monoid or a finite category.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The complete proof above was independently checked by the root and a second proof agent, including the strict image construction, the pointed-space localization triangle, and the fixed-weight multibar induction. The finite cellular control in \path{code/a_general_good_prime_control.py} checks the case where the ordinary union of two contractible regular-ideal images is a circle, while their pointed principal-ideal homotopy colimit is contractible. It verifies every action composition, chain-map equation, and strict quotient action in that example. This is a corroborating finite control, not the source of the all-order theorem. The proof makes no claim of literature priority and has no census-completeness dependency.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $N$ be a finite nilpotent semigroup with zero $0$, and let $I,J$ be finite nonempty sets with chosen elements $i_0,j_0$. Define \[ M=\{1\}\amalg(I\times J)\amalg(N\setminus\{0\}) \] as follows. The element $1$ is the identity, the set $I\times J$ is a rectangular-band ideal, and, writing $e=(i_0,j_0)$, \[ (i,j)(i',j')=(i,j'),\qquad n(i,j)=(i_0,j),\qquad (i,j)n=(i,j_0). \] For $n,n'\in N\setminus\{0\}$, their product is their product in $N$ if that is nonzero, and is $e$ otherwise. Then $M$ is an aperiodic finite monoid, and for every prime $p$ its cohomology $H^*(BM;\mathbb F_p)$ is locally finite as a module over the Steenrod algebra. In particular $BM$ is not homotopy equivalent to $\Sigma\CP^\infty$. More precisely, let $Q=N^1$ be the pointed monoid with zero as basepoint and a freshly adjoined identity, and let $\epsilon:Q\to S^0=\{*,1\}$ send all nonunits to the basepoint. Let $X_N$ be the based two-sided simplicial bar $B(S^0,Q,S^0)$ for this augmentation, with smash products in its levels. There is a stable equivalence \[ \widetilde{\Sigma^\infty BM}\ \simeq \bigvee^{(|I|-1)(|J|-1)}\Sigma^2\Sigma^\infty X_N. \tag{E.20} \] Every reduced cohomology class of $X_N$ is pulled back from a finite CW quotient of $X_N$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The theorem includes the inflated rectangular-band infinite-wedge example (one nonzero nilpotent letter with square zero). Its proof does not assume bounded homology or finite-dimensional homotopy type. It proves local finiteness for the stated family, not for all aperiodic monoids or all finite categories. The next subsection removes the constant-action hypothesis and allows a finite unit group at suitable primes. Further nonzero idempotents in a general Rees quotient require a separate argument; the controlled-image localization and multibar induction of Theorem~\ref{E:general-controlled-multibar} provide it below.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ be a finite monoid whose minimal ideal is a rectangular band $K=I\times J$. Write $Q=M/K$ for the pointed Rees quotient, with the entire ideal identified to its zero. For a finite nonempty set $I$ with chosen element $0$, let $F_I$ be the free group on symbols $x_i$ for $i\ne0$, and set $x_0=1$. A set map $\sigma:I\to I$ induces the group homomorphism \[ \Phi_\sigma(x_i)=x_{\sigma(0)}^{-1}x_{\sigma(i)}. \tag{E.26} \] The row actions of $M$ on $I$ give a pointed left $Q$-action on $BF_I$, and the column actions give a pointed right $Q$-action on $BF_J$. There is a stable equivalence \[ \widetilde{\Sigma^\infty BM}\simeq \Sigma^\infty B(BF_J,Q,BF_I). \tag{E.27} \] Here the bar is the \emph{pointed, smash-product} two-sided bar: its degree-$n$ space is $BF_J\wedge Q^{\wedge n}\wedge BF_I$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: For $S\subseteq I$, put $H_S=\langle x_a^{-1}x_b:a,b\in S\rangle\leq F_I$, with $H_\varnothing=1$. Then \[ \operatorname{im}\Phi_\sigma=H_{\sigma(I)},\qquad H_S\cap H_T=H_{S\cap T}. \tag{E.30} \] Every finite union of the nerve subcomplexes $BH_S\subset BF_I$ has finite CW homotopy type. The same holds for finite unions of products or smash products of such subcomplexes, and for cofibers of inclusions between these unions.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ be a finite monoid with rectangular-band minimal ideal $K$. Suppose its pointed Rees quotient is $Q=N^1$, where $N$ is a finite nilpotent semigroup with zero and the identity is freshly adjoined. No fixed-row or fixed-column hypothesis is imposed on the outside actions. Then, for every prime $p$, $H^*(BM;\mathbb F_p)$ is locally finite over the Steenrod algebra. In particular $BM\not\simeq \Sigma\CP^\infty$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: This theorem extends the constant-action inflation family. Its proof alone does not give Steenrod local finiteness for all finite aperiodic monoids. Nonzero idempotents in the Rees quotient prevent the positive weight used above. Extending the argument to further regular ideal layers requires additional coherent control of the endpoint module spectra; an ordinary monoid-algebra composition series does not provide it. The strictification in Lemma~\ref{E:regular-controlled-localization} supplies this control, and Theorem~\ref{E:general-controlled-multibar} proves the general result below.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $Q$ be a finite pointed monoid with group of units $G$, and let $Y,X$ be pointed simplicial sets with right and left $Q$-actions. Suppose the action of $G$ is by simplicial automorphisms. Form the ordinary pointed relative bar \[ C_n=Y\wedge_G Q\wedge_G\cdots\wedge_G Q\wedge_G X \tag{E.35} \] with $n$ middle copies of $Q$. The balancing is ordinary orbit balancing, not derived balancing. If $p\nmid|G|$, the canonical map \[ B(Y,Q,X)\longrightarrow |C_\bullet| \tag{E.36} \] is an $\mathbb F_p$-homology equivalence. It is an actual map of pointed spaces, and hence its cohomology isomorphism commutes with all Steenrod operations.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ have rectangular-band minimal ideal $K$, and suppose $Q=M/K$ is the disjoint union of a finite group of units $G$ and a nilpotent ideal $N$ with zero. At every prime $p\nmid|G|$, $H^*(BM;\mathbb F_p)$ is locally finite over the Steenrod algebra. In particular $BM\not\simeq\Sigma\CP^\infty$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ be a finite monoid whose only regular $\mathcal J$-classes are its minimal ideal and its group of units (allowing these to coincide). Let $H$ be a maximal subgroup in the minimal ideal and $G$ the unit group. If $p\nmid |G||H|$, then $H^*(BM;\mathbb F_p)$ is locally finite over the Steenrod algebra. Consequently no such monoid has classifying space $\Sigma\CP^\infty$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $B$ be a finite regular pointed monoid, with its zero as basepoint, and put $R_B=\Sigma^\infty B$. Let $p$ divide none of the orders of its nonzero maximal subgroups. If $L,V$ are a right and a left $R_B$-module with finite-dimensional total $\mathbb F_p$-homology, then $L\wedge_{R_B}^{\mathbb L}V$ also has finite-dimensional total $\mathbb F_p$-homology.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $M$ be a finite monoid with rectangular-band minimal ideal $K$. Suppose the pointed Rees quotient $Q=M/K$ has a nilpotent two-sided ideal $N$ containing zero such that $Q/N$ is a regular pointed monoid. No section of $Q\to Q/N$ is assumed. If $p$ divides none of the orders of the nonzero maximal subgroups of $Q/N$, then $H^*(BM;\mathbb F_p)$ is locally finite over the Steenrod algebra. In particular $BM\not\simeq\Sigma\CP^\infty$. For a minimal Rees matrix ideal over a finite group $H$, the same conclusion holds provided also that $p\nmid|H|$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: This theorem includes the split regular-submonoid situation $Q=B\cup N$, $B\cap N=\{0\}$, as well as the earlier finite-unit case. Its hypothesis still restricts the ideal structure. A nonregular element may have a nonzero regular element below it in the $\mathcal J$-order, preventing the nonregular elements from lying in a nilpotent ideal. Removing additional regular ideals preserves finite underlying endpoint spectra, but does not by itself supply the finite image filtrations (E.44) for their coherent quotient actions. The principal-ideal homotopy-colimit construction of Lemma~\ref{E:regular-controlled-localization} provides that additional step. The resulting general theorem and the finite-category reduction are proved in the following subsections.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Published homology prefilter and independently checked operations: Using the complete corner-irreducible monoid census and its published integral homology through degree seven in orders at most nine and through degree five in order ten, no monoid of order at most ten has classifying space homotopy equivalent to $\Sigma\CP^\infty$. The first monoid order not excluded by this calculation is eleven. The general exclusion in Corollary~\ref{E:Sigma-CP-infty-excluded} below is independent of this published prefilter and covers arbitrary finite monoids and categories.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Cup-product nilpotence does not obstruct a suspension, whose positive-degree products vanish. The finite operation certificates above do not by themselves establish an all-order assertion. Corollary~\ref{E:general-good-prime-LF} supplies the separate general Steenrod-module theorem, and Corollary~\ref{E:Sigma-CP-infty-excluded} settles the realization question negatively for both finite monoids and finite categories.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A group above a rectangular band: Let $G$ be a finite group, $I$ a nonempty finite left $G$-set, and $J$ a nonempty finite right $G$-set. On \[ M=G\amalg(I\times J) \] retain the multiplication of $G$ and define \[ (i,j)(i',j')=(i,j'),\qquad g(i,j)=(gi,j),\qquad (i,j)g=(i,jg). \] This is a finite regular monoid. Give $I*J$ the left $G$-action induced by $g i=gi$ and $g j=jg^{-1}$. There is a homotopy equivalence \[ BM\simeq\operatorname{hocofib} \bigl(EG\times_G(I*J)\longrightarrow BG\bigr), \] where the displayed map is the bundle projection. In particular this is a homotopy-type assertion in every degree, not an inference from initial homology groups.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The three two-point actions: Let $G=C_2$ and let each of $I,J$ have two elements. Up to interchanging left and right, the corresponding monoids in Theorem~\ref{E:group-band-cofiber} have the following homotopy types: \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \text{action on }I&\text{action on }J&\text{bundle over }\mathbb RP^\infty &BM\\\hline \text{trivial}&\text{trivial}&\varepsilon\oplus\varepsilon &S^2\vee\Sigma^2\mathbb RP^\infty\\ \text{trivial}&\text{interchange}&\varepsilon\oplus\gamma &\Sigma\mathbb RP^\infty\\ \text{interchange}&\text{interchange}&\gamma\oplus\gamma &\mathbb RP^\infty/\mathbb RP^1 \end{array} \] Here $\gamma$ is the tautological real line bundle and $\varepsilon$ the trivial real line bundle. These are, respectively, the supplied six-element classes $138,152,190$; changing the single nontrivial action from $J$ to $I$ gives the opposite of class $152$ and the same homotopy type. All three monoids have trivial universal group.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Finite certificates and their scope: The verification code is included as \texttt{a\_small\_infinite.py}. It checks all four pairs of two-point actions. It verifies the monoid tables, every defined composition and associativity equation of the three-object comparison category and its two-object Karoubi category, the comparison functor, both comma categories, their displayed initial objects and their point-intersection decomposition. It also records exact table isomorphisms with classes $138,152,190$ or their opposites. The output is \texttt{code/outputs/a\_small\_infinite.json}. These finite checks certify the category data used in the proof; the all-degree homotopy identifications follow from the preceding arguments, not from finite truncations of the nerve.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Every monoid of order at most six has exactly one of the homotopy types in the following table. The entries count isomorphism-or-opposite classes of monoids of the indicated order, not homotopy types or labelled tables. Thus every small monoid with unbounded homology is identified in all degrees, as requested in E5. \[ \begin{array}{l|rrrrrr} \text{homotopy type}&1&2&3&4&5&6\\\hline * & 1 & 1 & 4 & 19 & 126 & 1159 \\ S^2 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ BC_2 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 & 22 & 172 \\ BC_3 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 & 22 \\ BC_4 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ B(C_2\times C_2) & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ BC_5 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ BC_6 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ BS_3 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ S^2\vee\Sigma^2\RP^\infty & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ \Sigma\RP^\infty & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ \RP^\infty/\RP^1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ \bigvee_{n\geq2}S^n & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ \hline \text{total}&1&2&6&27&156&1373 \end{array} \]
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The three nongroup regular infinite types have zero positive cup products in the first two cases $S^2\vee\Sigma^2\RP^\infty$ and $\Sigma\RP^\infty$. In the third case \[ H^*(\RP^\infty/\RP^1;\F_2) \cong\F_2\oplus t^2\F_2[t],\qquad |t|=1. \] Its integral degree-two generator has every power nonzero; powers of exponent at least two have order two.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: B.8 at the finite bound: Let $\mathcal C$ be a skeleton of finite categories in $\Cat_{\mathrm{hot}}$, and localize it at nerve equivalences. A presheaf $F$ on this localization is the restriction of an ind-object invariant on finite tests if and only if its pullback has the following properties: $F(\varnothing)=*$, it takes finite disjoint unions to products, and, for every $u,v:A\rightrightarrows B$, the map \[ F(C)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Eq}(F(B)\rightrightarrows F(A)) \] is onto, where $C$ is the finite Grothendieck homotopy coequalizer of $u,v$. Every such restriction admits finite stages. This does not assert global invariance of that presentation on arbitrary small tests.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: B.9, including its strict idempotent step: A filtered ind-object of $\Cat_{\mathrm{hot}}$ with at most $m$ arrows at every stage is isomorphic to a constant category with at most $m$ arrows.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: C.22: exactly the strict colimit assertion: For full subcategory inclusions $K_0\subset K_1\subset\cdots$ and a category $X$ with finitely many objects, the canonical functor \[ \colim_n\operatorname{Fun}(X,K_n)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Fun}(X,\colim_n K_n) \] is an isomorphism. For an arbitrary filtered diagram, it is an isomorphism if $X$ has finitely many arrows. The corresponding assertion on components holds. These statements do not identify components with derived mapping classes.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: C.25 checked by explicit prisms: Weak-equivalence invariance of the constant-endpoint localization functor can fail for a finite relative category, even with all arrows marked, and for an equivalence between finite test categories.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The five-arrow counterexample in C.26: There is a nontrivial finite pointed relative category satisfying all three printed tests at IX ms.~22--23, including global invariance and both loop and suspension formulas.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Let $\mathrm{Hot}_0$ be the full subcategory of homotopy types represented by finite categories. It contains every finite CW homotopy type and strictly more, but does not contain $K(\Z,2)$, $K(\Z/2,2)$, or $\Omega S^3$. For connected finite CW complexes, its one-object part consists exactly of the simply connected types. Restricted unpointed set-valued tests $X\mapsto([BC,X])_{C\text{ finite}}$ are neither faithful nor conservative.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Finiteness of the arrow set does not make $BC$ a compact homotopy test. In particular the canonical comparison \[ \colim_r[\RP^\infty,\RP^r]\longrightarrow [\RP^\infty,\RP^\infty] \] is not surjective, although $\RP^\infty=BC_2$ for a finite category.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: For a finite category $C$ and a fixed degree $n$, integral homology $H_n(BC;\Z)$ is determined by a finite exact integer calculation. The fundamental group has an effectively given finite presentation. Neither statement is an algorithm deciding all homotopy questions about finite categories, in particular triviality of their fundamental groups.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The parallel-pair category has $4$ arrows and type $S^1$. The category $Z$ drawn at XII Appendix ms.~10--11 has $4$ objects, $10$ arrows, and type $S^2$, with $\pi_1(BZ)=0$ and $\pi_2(BZ)=\Z$. It does not retract onto its parallel-pair subcategory. The least arrow counts for $S^1,S^2,S^3$ are $4,5,7$, respectively; the $S^3$ models of size seven are exactly the four monoids in Section~\ref{sec:C}.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The replacement at XII Appendix ms.~15: For the displayed category $V'_0=Z$, replace the claim ``$\pi_1\cong\Z$'' by $\pi_1=0$, $\pi_2\cong\Z$. The proposed reason for non-asphericity for $W\subseteq W_1$ is false. A valid sufficient containment for this particular example is $W\subseteq W_2$ (in particular $W\subseteq W_\infty$).
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: An independent groupoid-suspension replacement for C.15: Let $G$ be a nontrivial group. There is a marked ordinary category with a globally invariant diagram-localization presheaf on all small tests whose infinity localization has a mapping space $BG$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Step audit of INDLOCAL C.27 and PRETOT F.1/F.4: For a small index category $A$, the canonical functor \[ \int_A D\longrightarrow\colim_A^{\Cat}D \] is a nerve weak equivalence for every functor $D:A\to\Cat$ if and only if every connected component of $A$ is filtered. The empty index is included. In particular the sequential indices in the cited manuscript passages satisfy the criterion, whereas the opposite type category does not.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Invariant paths with a nonlocal actual union: Let $C$ have objects $0,1$, identities, and two distinct arrows $f,g:0\to1$, and mark all its arrows. For every small category $Y$, the constant-endpoint localization functor is naturally \[ H_{0,0}(Y)= \Hom_{C^Y[\operatorname{Mor}(C^Y)^{-1}]}(0_Y,0_Y) \cong\{v:\pi_0Y\to\mathbb Z\mid v\text{ has finite image}\}. \] It is invariant under every nerve weak equivalence. Nevertheless, the actual symmetric alternating path union is not local and is not categorically homotopy equivalent to a local category. Its specified comparison on an infinite discrete test omits functions of infinite image. This supplies the two C.17 assertions used in C.28 directly.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The no-small-quotients resolution used by INDLOCAL: For a connected CW complex $W$ and an infinite cardinal $\lambda$ at least its number of cells, there is an acyclic map $t:BG\to W$ with $|G|\leq\lambda$ such that every homomorphism from $G$ to a group of cardinality less than $\lambda$ kills $\ker\pi_1(t)$. Here acyclic means an isomorphism in homology with every local coefficient system on $W$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The global ind-groupoid comparison used in C.28: Let $K:I\to\Cat_{\mathrm{hot}}$ be a small filtered diagram. If $H(X)=\colim_i\pi_0\operatorname{Fun}(X,K_i)$ inverts every nerve weak equivalence between small categories, then the canonical ind-morphism $(K_i)\to(\Pi_1K_i)$ is an isomorphism. The global quantifier on tests is essential.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: C.28: the finite-test comparison under global invariance: Suppose a sequence $(K_n)$ has globally invariant ind-presheaf $H$ as above. Put $Z=\hocolim_n BK_n$ and $\Gamma=\colim_n\Pi_1K_n$. The canonical map $Z\to B\Gamma$ is a homotopy equivalence. For every finite category $Y$ the specified map \[ c_Y:H(Y)\longrightarrow[BY,Z] \] is a bijection. The same conclusion holds when $\Pi_1Y$ is finitely presented. This is the valid finite-category formula at VII ms.~129--132, under the global invariance premise of that paragraph.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The required diagram-localization sphere test: Let $\mathcal M$ be bounded finite-dimensional rational chain complexes, marked at quasi-isomorphisms, and let $P$ be a finite poset. For constant diagrams $A=\Q[0]$, $B=\Q[2]$, there is a specified isomorphism \[ \Hom_{\mathcal M^P[\Sigma_P^{-1}]}(A_P,B_P) \cong H^2(BP;\Q). \] In particular the values for a finite face poset of $S^2$ and for a point are $\Q$ and the zero group, respectively.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: C.26: the loop formulas do not imply global invariance: The countable category of bounded finite-dimensional rational chain complexes, marked at quasi-isomorphisms, satisfies both pointed loop and suspension formulas but fails the global invariance condition of IX.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The marked comparison and its marking hypothesis: There is a natural weak equivalence, expressed by the canonical Grothendieck and reduction zigzag, \[ B\mathcal W(M;a,b)\simeq \operatorname{Map}_{L(M,\Sigma)}(a,b). \] It respects concatenation. This statement holds for the marking convention just specified.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: A relative interval contracts all arbitrary-vertical paths: Give $I_\tau$ the marking generated by its negative edges. Every nonempty category $F_\rho(0,|\tau|)$ of relative paths in this interval, with arbitrary endpoint-fixed transformations, is categorically contractible. It is nonempty exactly when there is a type map $\rho\to\tau$. Consequently $B\mathcal A(I_\tau)$ is contractible. If $t$ is universally cofinal in the reachability sense of C.20, then $B\mathcal E_t(I_\tau)$ is contractible as well.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The missing C.3/C.7 comparisons, with specified maps: For every small $(M,\Sigma)$ and every pair of endpoints the inclusion \[ B\mathcal W(M;a,b)\longrightarrow B\mathcal A(M;a,b) \] is a weak equivalence. For every universally cofinal actual projective sequence $t$, both maps in the specified span \[ B\colim_n F_{t_n}(a,b)\ \longleftarrow\ B\mathcal E_t(M;a,b)\ \longrightarrow\ B\mathcal A(M;a,b) \] are weak equivalences. These give the asserted localization mapping space and its compatibility with composition. In particular the path-model prerequisites of the supplied C.28 are valid with arbitrary interior vertical arrows, under the exact marking convention of C.20.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: Checking the projective-sequence classification C.21: For an actual projective sequence of types $t_n$, let $r_n$ count its nonempty constant-sign runs. The following are equivalent: $r_n$ is unbounded; every type receives a map from some $t_n$; and the all-small-test formula in Proposition~\ref{F:C20-paths} holds for every relative category and endpoint pair. If these conditions fail, the tail of the path diagram is isomorphic in $\Cat_{\mathrm{hot}}$ to the constant diagram at one finite alternating type. The identifications commute with the actual transition maps and localization effects.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: One-sign paths and the exact universal comparison: For any positive length, the all-positive endpoint-fixed path category is categorically homotopy equivalent to the discrete set $\Hom_M(a,b)$. The all-negative one is equivalent to the discrete set $\Sigma(b,a)$. These identifications commute with every same-sign type pullback after passage to $\Cat_{\mathrm{hot}}$, and hence hold after applying $\pi_0\operatorname{Fun}(X,-)$ for every small $X$. The comparison of positive paths with localization mapping spaces is an equivalence at all endpoints exactly when every marked arrow is already an isomorphism in $M$. For negative paths the analogous all-endpoint condition is that $M$ is a groupoid and $\Sigma=\operatorname{Mor}M$. At one endpoint pair the exact condition is that the specified effect map is bijective on components and every component of the localization mapping space is contractible. In particular, when all arrows are marked, the positive comparison holds everywhere exactly for groupoids.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The type-map contraction: A type is a finite word $\sigma$ in $+,-$, including the empty word. Its interval $I_\sigma$ is the free category on the oriented line with vertices $0,\ldots,|\sigma|$. Maps of types are endpoint-preserving, nondecreasing functors of these intervals. For fixed $\sigma,\tau$, the category $P(\sigma,\tau)$ of such functors and endpoint-fixed natural transformations is either empty or categorically contractible: its identity is connected to a constant functor by a finite zigzag of natural transformations.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The uniform fibred comparison used in C.28: For $u:J\to T$, the map of fibred Grothendieck constructions \[ \int_J^{\mathrm{fib}}F u^{\op}\longrightarrow \int_T^{\mathrm{fib}}F \] is a nerve weak equivalence for every strict $F:T^{\op}\to\Cat$ if and only if each comma $u/t$ is weakly contractible. Parallel pullback homotopies and a cofinal reachability sequence alone do not imply this condition. In particular they do not justify the universal comparison proposed at VII ms.~99--110.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: C.22, the remaining type and colimit assertions: Concatenation of types and their interval functors is strictly associative and unital. The empty type is terminal. The opposite type category is neither filtered nor totally $W_\infty$-aspherical. Nevertheless every actual projective sequence of types gives a covariant path diagram indexed by the filtered category $\N$; its ordinary categorical colimit has the homotopy type of its homotopy colimit. Together with Proposition~\ref{F:C22}, these statements check all assertions of \textup{\textsc{INDLOCAL}} C.22.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The first proof of C.20, with its missing prerequisite supplied: Let $(M,\Sigma)$ be a small relative category with all identities and composites in its marking. Let $t:\N^{\op}\to\mathrm{Ty}$ be an actual sequence such that every type receives a map from some $t_n$. Write $K_n=F_{t_n}(a,b)$ for paths with marked negative edges, arbitrary interior vertical arrows, and identity endpoint components. For every small category $X$, including infinite and empty ones, effect of words gives a natural bijection \[ \colim_n\pi_0\operatorname{Fun}(X,K_n) \cong \Hom_{M^X[\Sigma_X^{-1}]}(a_X,b_X). \] Here $\Sigma_X$ consists of the pointwise marked transformations. The comparison respects constant paths, concatenation, and restriction in $X$.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The positive presentation assertions in C.28: A globally invariant sequential ind-object admits a presentation by full inclusions of local Thomason-fibrant categories. The union is Thomason-fibrant. It need not be local or represent the ind-object. Filtered colimits of Thomason-fibrant categories are fibrant, and objectwise weak equivalences of filtered diagrams induce weak equivalences of their colimits.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The union and uniqueness counterexample in C.24/C.28: There is a sequence of finite local fibrant categories with full inclusions whose fibrant union $T$ is not local. It has an endofunctor $s$ equal to the identity as an ind-morphism in $\operatorname{Ind}(\Cat_{\mathrm{hot}})$ but not a nerve weak equivalence. Thus ind-isomorphisms do not give the asserted uniqueness of unions at V ms.~46--49.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.

statement: The representation and retraction qualifications in C.28: For full-inclusion sequences, an ind-morphism in $\Cat$ is exactly a functor on unions whose restriction to each source stage lands in some target stage. Equality in $\operatorname{Ind}(\Cat_{\mathrm{hot}})$ does not imply equality or homotopy of the induced union functors. A globally invariant ind-object is represented in $\Cat_{\mathrm{hot}}$ exactly when it is isomorphic to a constant ind-object. If $A$ is Thomason-fibrant, $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ is a Thomason cofibration, and $p:B\to A$ has $pi$ categorically homotopic to $1_A$, there is a strict retraction $r$ in the same ordinary homotopy class as $p$. If $A$ is also local, the equality holds in $\Cat_{\mathrm{hot}}$. For a groupoid target the latter assertion holds for any full inclusion injective on objects.
notes: Numbered statement; LaTeX labels are stable identifiers.
